# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Your WorkOS API key prefixed with `sk_`. Pass it as a Bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer sk_example_123456789`.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer An SSO access token returned from the Get a Profile and Token endpoint.

<h1 id="workos-admin-portal">admin-portal</h1>

Endpoints for the Admin Portal API.

## Generate a Portal Link

<a id="opIdPortalSessionsController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/portal/generate_link \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "return_url": "https://example.com/admin-portal/return",
    "success_url": "https://example.com/admin-portal/success",
    "organization": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "external_user_id": "user_12345",
    "intent": "sso",
    "it_contact_emails": [
      "it-contact@example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /portal/generate_link`

Generate a Portal Link scoped to an Organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "return_url": "https://example.com/admin-portal/return",
  "success_url": "https://example.com/admin-portal/success",
  "organization": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "external_user_id": "user_12345",
  "intent": "sso",
  "it_contact_emails": [
    "it-contact@example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-portal-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[GenerateLinkDto](#schemageneratelinkdto)|true|none|
|» return_url|body|string|false|The URL to go to when an admin clicks on your logo in the Admin Portal. If not specified, the return URL configured on the [Admin Portal](https://dashboard.workos.com/admin-portal) page will be used.|
|» success_url|body|string|false|The URL to redirect the admin to when they finish setup. If not specified, the success URL configured on the [Admin Portal](https://dashboard.workos.com/admin-portal) page will be used.|
|» organization|body|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|» external_user_id|body|string|false|The ID of the user in your application the link is generated for. The link and any Admin Portal sessions started from it can later be revoked by this ID, for example when that user is deprovisioned from your application.|
|» intent|body|string|false|<br>      The intent of the Admin Portal.<br>        - `sso` - Launch Admin Portal for creating SSO connections<br>        - `dsync` - Launch Admin Portal for creating Directory Sync connections<br>        - `audit_logs` - Launch Admin Portal for viewing Audit Logs<br>        - `log_streams` - Launch Admin Portal for creating Log Streams<br>        - `domain_verification` - Launch Admin Portal for Domain Verification<br>        - `certificate_renewal` - Launch Admin Portal for renewing SAML Certificates<br>        - `bring_your_own_key` - Launch Admin Portal for configuring Bring Your Own Key|
|» it_contact_emails|body|[string(email)]|false|The email addresses of the IT contacts to grant access to the Admin Portal for the given organization. Accepts up to 20 emails.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» intent|sso|
|» intent|dsync|
|» intent|audit_logs|
|» intent|log_streams|
|» intent|domain_verification|
|» intent|certificate_renewal|
|» intent|bring_your_own_key|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

## Revoke a Portal Link

<a id="opIdPortalSessionsController_revokeLink"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/portal/revoke_link \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "organization": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "external_user_id": "user_12345"
  }'
```

`POST /portal/revoke_link`

Revokes every Portal Link generated for the given organization with the given `external_user_id`, and immediately ends any Admin Portal sessions that were started from those links. Use this when an admin is deprovisioned from your application: unopened links stop working, and their already-open portal sessions are ended. Only links that were generated with an `external_user_id` can be revoked, so pass one to `generate_link` for every admin you may later need to deprovision.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "external_user_id": "user_12345"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-portal-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[RevokeLinkDto](#schemarevokelinkdto)|true|none|
|» organization|body|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|» external_user_id|body|string|true|The `external_user_id` the Portal Links were generated with for this organization. Every matching link is revoked, along with any Admin Portal sessions started from those links.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-a-portal-link-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

<h1 id="workos-agentsblueprints">agents.blueprints</h1>

## List agent blueprints

<a id="opIdAgentBlueprintsController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/blueprints \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /agents/blueprints`

Lists the agent blueprints in the current environment.

<h3 id="list-agent-blueprints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
  "object": "list",

    "after": "agent_blueprint_01HXYZ987654321KJIHGFEDCBA"
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "agent_blueprint",
      "id": "agent_blueprint_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "name": "Prospecting Agent",
      "description": "Finds and qualifies sales prospects.",

        "crm:read",
        "email:send"
      ],
      "invocable_by": {
        "role_slugs": [
          "manager"
        ],
        "organization_ids": [
          "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY"
        ]
      },
      "invocable_as": {
        "instance_types": [
          "delegated",
          "autonomous"
        ]
      },
      "session_settings": {
        "max_age_seconds": 3600,

      },
      "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
```

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

<h3 id="list-agent-blueprints-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|false|none|Indicates this is a list response.|
|list_metadata|object|false|none|Pagination cursors for navigating between pages of results.|
|» before|string \| null|true|none|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the start of the list.|
|» after|string \| null|true|none|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list.|
|data|[[AgentBlueprint](#schemaagentblueprint)]|false|none|The list of records for the current page.|

## Create an agent blueprint

<a id="opIdAgentBlueprintsController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/blueprints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Prospecting Agent",
    "description": "Finds and qualifies sales prospects.",
    "permissions": [
      "crm:read",
      "email:send"
    ],
    "invocable_by": {},
    "invocable_as": {},
    "session_settings": {
      "max_age_seconds": 3600,
      "access_token_ttl_seconds": 300,
      "refresh_token_ttl_seconds": 3600
    }
  }'
```

`POST /agents/blueprints`

Creates an agent blueprint: the template describing what an agent may do (its permission ceiling), who may invoke it, and the lifetimes of its sessions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Prospecting Agent",
  "description": "Finds and qualifies sales prospects.",
  "permissions": [
    "crm:read",
    "email:send"
  ],
  "invocable_by": {},
  "invocable_as": {},
  "session_settings": {
    "max_age_seconds": 3600,
    "access_token_ttl_seconds": 300,
    "refresh_token_ttl_seconds": 3600
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-agent-blueprint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name of the agent blueprint.|
|» description|body|string|false|Human-readable description of the agent blueprint.|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|Permission slugs forming the ceiling on what sessions minted from this blueprint may do. Each slug must exist in the environment.|
|» invocable_by|body|object|false|Who may mint sessions from this blueprint.|
|» » role_slugs|body|[string]|false|Role slugs whose members may mint user-delegated sessions from this blueprint. An empty list allows any member.|
|» » organization_ids|body|[string]|false|Organizations in which sessions may be minted from this blueprint, enforced on user-delegated, autonomous, and agent-delegated mints. An empty list allows any organization in the environment.|
|» invocable_as|body|object|false|How sessions may be minted from this blueprint.|
|» » instance_types|body|[string]|false|Instance types that may be minted from this blueprint: `delegated` (a user-delegated session, minted with a user access token) and/or `autonomous` (a session acting as the agent itself, minted with an agent registration credential). Agent-delegated chaining and refreshes are checked against the type of the presenting instance. Defaults to both.|
|» session_settings|body|object|false|Token and session lifetimes for sessions minted from this blueprint.|
|» » max_age_seconds|body|integer|true|Maximum lifetime of a session in seconds; refreshes never extend a session past this. At most 31,536,000 (365 days).|
|» » access_token_ttl_seconds|body|integer|true|Lifetime of each minted access token in seconds. At most 3,600 (1 hour).|
|» » refresh_token_ttl_seconds|body|integer|true|Lifetime of each rotated refresh token in seconds. At most 5,184,000 (60 days).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » instance_types|delegated|
|» » instance_types|autonomous|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "object": "agent_blueprint",
  "id": "agent_blueprint_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "name": "Prospecting Agent",

    ]
  },

    "instance_types": [
      "delegated",

    ]
  },
  "session_settings": {
    "max_age_seconds": 3600,
    "access_token_ttl_seconds": 300,
    "refresh_token_ttl_seconds": 3600
  },
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```bash
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /agents/blueprints/{agent_blueprint_id}`

Updates an agent blueprint. Omitted fields are left unchanged; provided lists replace the existing configuration.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Prospecting Agent",
  "description": "Finds and qualifies sales prospects.",
  "permissions": [
    "crm:read",
    "email:send"
  ],
  "invocable_by": {
    "role_slugs": [
      "manager"
    ],
    "organization_ids": [
      "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY"
    ]
  },
  "invocable_as": {
    "instance_types": [
      "delegated",
      "autonomous"
    ]
  },
  "session_settings": {
    "max_age_seconds": 3600,
    "access_token_ttl_seconds": 300,
    "refresh_token_ttl_seconds": 3600
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-agent-blueprint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_blueprint_id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the agent blueprint.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable name of the agent blueprint.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Human-readable description of the agent blueprint. Pass `null` to clear it.|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|Permission slugs forming the ceiling on what sessions minted from this blueprint may do. Each slug must exist in the environment.|
|» invocable_by|body|object|false|Who may mint sessions from this blueprint. Omitted lists are left unchanged.|
|» » role_slugs|body|[string]|false|Role slugs whose members may mint user-delegated sessions from this blueprint. An empty list allows any member.|
|» » organization_ids|body|[string]|false|Organizations in which sessions may be minted from this blueprint, enforced on user-delegated, autonomous, and agent-delegated mints. An empty list allows any organization in the environment.|
|» invocable_as|body|object|false|How sessions may be minted from this blueprint. Omitted lists are left unchanged.|
|» » instance_types|body|[string]|false|Instance types that may be minted from this blueprint: `delegated` and/or `autonomous`. At least one is required; existing sessions of a removed type are refused at their next refresh.|
|» session_settings|body|object|false|Token and session lifetimes for sessions minted from this blueprint. Omitted fields are left unchanged.|
|» » max_age_seconds|body|integer|false|Maximum lifetime of a session in seconds; refreshes never extend a session past this. At most 31,536,000 (365 days).|
|» » access_token_ttl_seconds|body|integer|false|Lifetime of each minted access token in seconds. At most 3,600 (1 hour).|
|» » refresh_token_ttl_seconds|body|integer|false|Lifetime of each rotated refresh token in seconds. At most 5,184,000 (60 days).|

#### Enumerated Values

|» » instance_types|delegated|
|» » instance_types|autonomous|

<h1 id="workos-agentsblueprintstokens">agents.blueprints.tokens</h1>

Mint and validate agent access tokens.

## Mint an agent token

<a id="opIdAgentBlueprintsTokenController_mintToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/blueprints/agent_blueprint_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY/tokens \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "user_delegated",
    "user_access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6...",
    "intent": "renew-contract-123"
  }'
```

`POST /agents/blueprints/{agent_blueprint_id}/tokens`

Mint an agent access token (and backing session) from an agent blueprint. The session can be user-delegated (exchanging a user access token), autonomous (the agent acting as itself in an organization), agent-delegated (the agent exchanging its own access token for a new session on the same instance), or a refresh of a previously issued refresh token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "user_delegated",
  "user_access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6...",
  "intent": "renew-contract-123"
}
```

<h3 id="mint-an-agent-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_blueprint_id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the agent blueprint.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|How the session is minted: `user_delegated`, `autonomous`, `agent_delegated`, or `refresh`.|
|» user_access_token|body|string|true|The access token of the user delegating to the agent. The token identifies the user and organization; effective permissions are resolved server-side.|
|» intent|body|string|false|Optional caller-supplied context, echoed as an object with a `text` field in the `intent` claim of the minted access token.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|How the session is minted: `user_delegated`, `autonomous`, `agent_delegated`, or `refresh`.|
|» organization_id|body|string|true|The organization the agent acts within when operating as itself.|
|» intent|body|string|false|Optional caller-supplied context, echoed as an object with a `text` field in the `intent` claim of the minted access token.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|How the session is minted: `user_delegated`, `autonomous`, `agent_delegated`, or `refresh`.|
|» agent_access_token|body|string|true|The agent's own access token to exchange for a new session on the same instance. The token must have been minted from this blueprint; permissions are re-derived from current authority.|
|» intent|body|string|false|Optional caller-supplied context, echoed as an object with a `text` field in the `intent` claim of the minted access token.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|How the session is minted: `user_delegated`, `autonomous`, `agent_delegated`, or `refresh`.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|true|The refresh token issued with a previous agent access token. Refresh tokens are single-use: each refresh rotates it.|
|» intent|body|string|false|Optional caller-supplied context, echoed as an object with a `text` field in the `intent` claim of the minted access token.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "refresh_token": "njGkA8Wyht0GBEGGA0Zh1Q3wZzL2...",
  "agent_instance_id": "agent_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "new_instance": false,
  "agent_instance_session_id": "agent_session_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "permissions": [
    "crm:read"
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="mint-an-agent-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AgentToken](#schemaagenttoken)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

## Validate an agent token

<a id="opIdAgentBlueprintsTokenController_validateToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/blueprints/agent_blueprint_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY/tokens/validate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "agent_access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6..."
  }'
```

`POST /agents/blueprints/{agent_blueprint_id}/tokens/validate`

Validates an agent access token: verifies its signature against the environment, that it was minted under this blueprint, and that the backing session is live (not revoked or expired, and — for delegated sessions — that the delegating user session has not ended). Returns the token claims and session metadata when valid; invalid tokens are reported as errors with stable codes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "agent_access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6..."
}
```

<h3 id="validate-an-agent-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_blueprint_id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the agent blueprint.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» agent_access_token|body|string|true|The agent access token (a JWT) to validate.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "agent_instance_id": "agent_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "agent_instance_session_id": "agent_session_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "permissions": [
    "crm:read"
  ],
  "intent": "renew-contract-123",
  "acting_user_id": "userland_user_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "session_expires_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="validate-an-agent-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AgentTokenValidation](#schemaagenttokenvalidation)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

</aside>

## List agent instances

<a id="opIdAgentInstancesController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/instances \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /agents/instances`

Lists the agent instances in the current environment. Instances are created implicitly when tokens are minted.

<h3 id="list-agent-instances-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Only return instances acting within this organization.|
|agent_blueprint_id|query|string|false|Only return instances minted from this blueprint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "list_metadata": {
    "before": "agent_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "after": "agent_01HXYZ987654321KJIHGFEDCBA"
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "agent_instance",
      "id": "agent_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "agent_blueprint_id": "agent_blueprint_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",

      "type": "delegated",
      "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

## Link a claim attempt to an external user

<a id="opIdAgentAdminController_linkClaimAttemptToExternalUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/claims/attempts \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "link_external_user",
    "claim_attempt_token": "cla_tkn_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
    "user": {
      "email": "alice@example.com",
      "external_id": "user_abc123"
    },
    "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY"
  }'
```

`PATCH /agents/claims/attempts`

Link an external user to a claim attempt and retrieve the code needed for the agent to complete the claim. The user is looked up by external ID; if no user exists, one is created. When the user belongs to multiple organizations, an explicit organization must be provided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "link_external_user",
  "claim_attempt_token": "cla_tkn_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "user": {
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "external_id": "user_abc123"
  },
  "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY"
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-claim-attempt-to-an-external-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The operation to perform on the claim attempt. Currently only `link_external_user` is supported.|
|» claim_attempt_token|body|string|true|The token identifying the claim attempt.|
|» user|body|object|true|The user to attach to the claim attempt, identified by email and external ID.|
|» » email|body|string(email)|true|The email address of the user.|
|» » external_id|body|string|true|The external ID of the user.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|The organization to place the agent in. Required when the user belongs to more than one organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "agent_reg_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "status": "unverified",
  "user_code": "BCDF-GHJK",
  "organizations": [
    {
      "id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "name": "Acme Corp"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
  "code": "organization_selection_required",
  "message": "Request could not be processed.",
  "organizations": [
    {
      "id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "name": "Acme Corp"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 410 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
```

## Validate an agent credential

<a id="opIdAgentAdminController_validateCredential"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/credentials/validate \
  -X POST \

    "type": "api_key",
```

`POST /agents/credentials/validate`

Validate an agent credential — an API key or access token — against the environment of the API key used to authenticate the request. This is a read-only check: it never consumes or mutates the credential.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "api_key",
  "credential": "sk_agent_example_1234567890"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-an-agent-credential-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The kind of credential being validated — an agent API key or an agent access token.|
|» credential|body|string(password)|true|The credential value to validate: the API key value for `api_key`, or the access token (JWT) for `access_token`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The kind of credential being validated — an agent API key or an agent access token.|
|» credential|body|string(password)|true|The credential value to validate: the API key value for `api_key`, or the access token (JWT) for `access_token`.|
|» audience|body|string|false|When provided, the access token's `aud` claim is verified against this value. Tokens issued for a different resource are rejected.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "valid": true,
  "registration_id": "agent_reg_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "expires_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /agents/registrations/{id}/revoke`

Revoke an agent registration by ID. Revocation is permanent: the registration, its identity assertions, and every access token or API key issued from it stop working, and the agent must register again. Revoking an already revoked registration succeeds and returns the original `revoked_at`. The registration is scoped to the environment of the API key used to authenticate the request.

<h3 id="revoke-an-agent-registration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the agent registration.|

|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|

## Revoke an agent instance session

<a id="opIdAgentInstanceSessionsController_revoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/agents/sessions/agent_session_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /agents/sessions/{agent_instance_session_id}/revoke`

Revokes an agent instance session, invalidating its refresh token and every access token minted under it. Revocation is idempotent: revoking an already-revoked session keeps the original `revoked_at`, and revoking an already-expired session returns the session with `status: expired` and a null `revoked_at`.

<h3 id="revoke-an-agent-instance-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|agent_instance_session_id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the agent instance session.|

```json
{
  "object": "agent_instance_session",

  "agent_instance_id": "agent_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "status": "active",
  "expires_at": "2026-01-15T13:00:00.000Z",
  "revoked_at": null,
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

```json
}
```

`GET /connect/applications`

List all Connect Applications in the current environment with optional filtering.

<h3 id="list-connect-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|registration_types|query|[string]|false|Filter Connect Applications by registration type. Specify multiple as a comma-separated list (e.g. `registration_types=dynamic,authenticated`). Defaults to `authenticated` only when not specified.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Filter Connect Applications by organization ID.|

`POST /audit_logs/events`

Create an Audit Log Event.

This API supports idempotency which guarantees that performing the same operation multiple times will have the same result as if the operation were performed only once. This is handy in situations where you may need to retry a request due to a failure or prevent accidental duplicate requests from creating more than one resource.

To achieve idempotency, you can add `Idempotency-Key` request header to a Create Event request with a unique string as the value. Each subsequent request matching this unique string will return the same response. We suggest using [v4 UUIDs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universally_unique_identifier) for idempotency keys to avoid collisions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "event": {
    "action": "user.signed_in",
    "occurred_at": "2026-02-02T16:35:39.317Z",
    "actor": {
      "id": "user_TF4C5938",
      "type": "user",
      "name": "Jon Smith",
      "metadata": {
        "owner": "user_01GBTCQ2"
      }
    },
    "targets": [
      {
        "id": "user_TF4C5938",
        "type": "user",
        "name": "Jon Smith",
        "metadata": {
          "owner": "user_01GBTCQ2"
        }
      }
    ],
    "context": {
      "location": "123.123.123.123",
      "user_agent": "Chrome/104.0.0.0"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "owner": "user_01GBTCQ2"
    },
    "version": 1
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|A unique string to prevent duplicate requests. Each subsequent request matching this unique string will return the same response. We suggest using v4 UUIDs.|
|body|body|[AuditLogEventIngestionDto](#schemaauditlogeventingestiondto)|true|none|
|» organization_id|body|string|true|The unique ID of the Organization.|
|» event|body|[AuditLogEventDto](#schemaauditlogeventdto)|true|The audit log event to create.|

> Example responses

```json
  "success": true
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "message": "Invalid Audit Log event.",
  "code": "invalid_audit_log_event",

    {
      "instancePath": "/targets"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",

}
```

```json
{

}
```

```json
    {
      "code": "required",

    }
  ]
}
```

`GET /authorization/groups/{group_id}/role_assignments`

List all role assignments granted to a group. Each assignment represents a role granted to the group on a resource.

<h3 id="list-role-assignments-for-a-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|group_id|path|string|true|The ID of the group.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

`PATCH /authorization/groups/{group_id}/role_assignments`

Add and remove role assignments for a group in a single atomic operation. Additions that already exist and removals that match no assignment are skipped. An assignment in both lists is rejected. `add` and `remove` must contain between 1 and 100 entries combined.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add": [
    {
      "role_slug": "admin"
    },
    {
      "role_slug": "member",
      "resource_id": "authz_resource_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGH"
    }
  ],
  "remove": [
    {
      "role_slug": "editor",
      "resource_type_slug": "project",
      "resource_external_id": "proj-789"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|group_id|path|string|true|The ID of the group.|
|body|body|[PatchGroupRoleAssignmentsDto](#schemapatchgrouproleassignmentsdto)|true|none|
|» add|body|[[ReplaceGroupRoleAssignmentEntryDto](#schemareplacegrouproleassignmententrydto)]|false|Role assignments to add to the group. Assignments that already exist are skipped.|
|» remove|body|[[ReplaceGroupRoleAssignmentEntryDto](#schemareplacegrouproleassignmententrydto)]|false|Role assignments to remove from the group. Entries that match no assignment are skipped.|

## List resources for organization membership

<a id="opIdAuthorizationController_listResourcesForMembership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/authorization/organization_memberships/om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/resources?permission_slug=project%3Aread' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /authorization/organization_memberships/{organization_membership_id}/resources`

Returns all child resources of a parent resource where the organization membership has a specific permission. This is useful for resource discovery—answering "What projects can this user access in this workspace?"

You must provide either `parent_resource_id` or both `parent_resource_external_id` and `parent_resource_type_slug` to identify the parent resource.

<h3 id="list-resources-for-organization-membership-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_membership_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization membership.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|permission_slug|query|string|true|The permission slug to filter by. Only child resources where the organization membership has this permission are returned.|
|parent_resource_id|query|string|false|The WorkOS ID of the parent resource. Provide this or both `parent_resource_external_id` and `parent_resource_type_slug`, but not both. Mutually exclusive with `parent_resource_type_slug` and `parent_resource_external_id`.|
|parent_resource_type_slug|query|string|false|The slug of the parent resource type. Must be provided together with `parent_resource_external_id`. Required with `parent_resource_external_id`. Mutually exclusive with `parent_resource_id`.|
|parent_resource_external_id|query|string|false|The application-specific external identifier of the parent resource. Must be provided together with `parent_resource_type_slug`. Required with `parent_resource_type_slug`. Mutually exclusive with `parent_resource_id`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
  "object": "list",

    {
      "object": "authorization_resource",
      "name": "Website Redesign",

      "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
      "parent_resource_id": "authz_resource_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",

    }
```

## List effective permissions for an organization membership on a resource

<a id="opIdAuthorizationController_listEffectivePermissions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/authorization/organization_memberships/om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/resources/authz_resource_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/permissions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /authorization/organization_memberships/{organization_membership_id}/resources/{resource_id}/permissions`

Returns all permissions the organization membership effectively has on a resource, including permissions inherited through roles assigned to ancestor resources. Results are not filtered by the resource type: a permission is returned whenever a check for it on this resource would be authorized, and each permission is labeled with the resource type it is declared on.

<h3 id="list-effective-permissions-for-an-organization-membership-on-a-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_membership_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization membership.|
|resource_id|path|string|true|The ID of the authorization resource.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. ## List effective permissions for an organization membership on a resource by external ID


`GET /authorization/organization_memberships/{organization_membership_id}/resources/{resource_type_slug}/{external_id}/permissions`

Returns all permissions the organization membership effectively has on a resource identified by its external ID, including permissions inherited through roles assigned to ancestor resources. Results are not filtered by the resource type: a permission is returned whenever a check for it on this resource would be authorized, and each permission is labeled with the resource type it is declared on.

For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|

`GET /authorization/resources/{resource_id}/organization_memberships`

<h3 id="list-organization-memberships-for-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|permission_slug|query|string|true|The permission slug to filter by. Only users with this permission on the resource are returned.|
|assignment|query|string|false|Filter by assignment type. Use `direct` for direct assignments only, or `indirect` to include inherited assignments.|

## Create a Connection

<a id="opIdConnectionsController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/connections \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
    "name": "Foo Corp",
    "external_id": "acme-legacy-conn-42",
    "connection_type": "OktaSAML",
    "attribute_maps": {
      "standard_attributes": {
        "idp_id": "sub",
        "email": "email",
        "first_name": "given_name",
        "last_name": "family_name",
        "groups": "memberOf",
        "name": "displayName"
      },
      "custom_attributes": {
        "company": "company_claim"
      }
    },
    "saml_options": {
      "idp_metadata_url": "https://idp.example.com/metadata.xml",
      "acs_url": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
      "sp_entity_id": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
      "idp_entity_id": "https://idp.example.com/entity",
      "idp_sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso",
      "idp_signing_certs": [
        "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
      ],
      "sp_signing_key_pair": {
        "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
        "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
      },
      "sp_encryption_key_pairs": [
        {
          "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
          "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`POST /connections`

Creates a new connection for an organization. Provide `saml_options` or `oidc_options` to configure the identity provider. When `external_id` matches an existing connection in the organization, that connection is returned instead of creating a duplicate.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "name": "Foo Corp",
  "external_id": "acme-legacy-conn-42",
  "connection_type": "OktaSAML",
  "attribute_maps": {
    "standard_attributes": {
      "idp_id": "sub",
      "email": "email",
      "first_name": "given_name",
      "last_name": "family_name",
      "groups": "memberOf",
      "name": "displayName"
    },
    "custom_attributes": {
      "company": "company_claim"
    }
  },
  "saml_options": {
    "idp_metadata_url": "https://idp.example.com/metadata.xml",
    "acs_url": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
    "sp_entity_id": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
    "idp_entity_id": "https://idp.example.com/entity",
    "idp_sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso",
    "idp_signing_certs": [
      "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    ],
    "sp_signing_key_pair": {
      "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    },
    "sp_encryption_key_pairs": [
      {
        "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
        "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateConnectionDto](#schemacreateconnectiondto)|true|none|
|» organization_id|body|string|true|Unique identifier for the Organization in which the Connection resides.|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for the Connection. This will most commonly be the organization's name.|
|» external_id|body|string|false|The customer-owned identifier for the Connection.|
|» connection_type|body|string|false|The type of the Connection. Only SAML and OIDC connection types may be created. When omitted, the type is inferred from the provided options.|
|» attribute_maps|body|[CreateConnectionAttributeMapsDto](#schemacreateconnectionattributemapsdto)|false|How IdP attributes or claims map onto WorkOS profile fields. Provided fields override the defaults for the connection type.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» saml_options|body|[CreateConnectionSamlOptionsDto](#schemacreateconnectionsamloptionsdto)|true|Protocol configuration for SAML connections. Mutually exclusive with `oidc_options`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» oidc_options|body|[CreateConnectionOidcOptionsDto](#schemacreateconnectionoidcoptionsdto)|true|Protocol configuration for OIDC connections. Mutually exclusive with `saml_options`.|

## Create an IdP signing certificate

<a id="opIdSamlIdpSigningCertificatesController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/connections/conn_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5/saml_idp_signing_certs \
```

`POST /connections/{connectionId}/saml_idp_signing_certs`

Adds an Identity Provider signing certificate to the connection, so SAML responses signed with its key can be verified. Use this to import a new certificate ahead of an Identity Provider rotation — the existing certificates keep working until they are deleted or expire.

> Body parameter

```json
  "value": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----MIIC...-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
}
```

## Create an SP encryption certificate

<a id="opIdSamlSpEncryptionCertificatesController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/connections/conn_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5/saml_sp_encryption_certs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /connections/{connectionId}/saml_sp_encryption_certs`

Generates a new encryption key pair for the connection and returns its public certificate. WorkOS holds the private key, so the request takes no body — to bring your own key pairs, provide `saml_options.sp_encryption_key_pairs` when creating the connection instead. Creating a certificate appends rather than replaces: every active private key is tried when decrypting, which lets a rotation overlap the old and new certificates.

<h3 id="create-an-sp-encryption-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectionId|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the Connection.|

```json
  "value": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----MIIC...-----END CERTIFICATE-----",
  "not_before": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "not_after": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

```json
}
```

`PATCH /connections/{id}`

Updates an existing connection. Only the provided fields are changed; fields that accept `null` are reset to their default behavior.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Foo Corp",
  "external_id": "acme-legacy-conn-42",
  "connection_type": "OktaSAML",
  "attribute_maps": {
    "standard_attributes": {
      "idp_id": "sub",
      "email": "email",
      "first_name": "given_name",
      "last_name": "family_name",
      "groups": "memberOf",
      "name": "displayName"
    },
    "custom_attributes": {
      "company": "company_claim"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the Connection.|
|body|body|[PatchConnectionDto](#schemapatchconnectiondto)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable name for the Connection.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|The customer-owned identifier for the Connection. Set to `null` to stop tracking one.|
|» connection_type|body|string|false|The type of the Connection. Immutable after creation — it may be sent, but only with the Connection current type.|
|» attribute_maps|body|[PatchConnectionAttributeMapsDto](#schemapatchconnectionattributemapsdto)|false|How IdP attributes or claims map onto WorkOS profile fields. Only the provided fields are updated.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» saml_options|body|[PatchConnectionSamlOptionsDto](#schemapatchconnectionsamloptionsdto)|true|Protocol configuration for SAML connections. Only the provided fields are updated. Mutually exclusive with `oidc_options`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» oidc_options|body|[PatchConnectionOidcOptionsDto](#schemapatchconnectionoidcoptionsdto)|true|Protocol configuration for OIDC connections. Only the provided fields are updated. Mutually exclusive with `saml_options`.|

`GET /directories`

Get a list of all of your existing directories matching the criteria specified.

<h3 id="list-directories-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Defaults to `normal`.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Filter Directories by their associated organization.|
|search|query|string|false|Searchable text to match against Directory names.|
|domain|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Filter Directories by their associated domain.|

## Sync a Directory

<a id="opIdDirectoriesController_syncDirectory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/directories/directory_01ECAZ4NV9QMV47GW873HDCX74/sync \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /directories/{id}/sync`

Request an asynchronous sync from the directory provider. Currently supports Google Workspace directories in linked or validating state. Manual requests share a five-minute per-directory cooldown across the API, Dashboard, Admin Portal, and MCP. Acceptance means the request was queued, not that the sync has started or completed. A running sync prevents another request from being queued.

<h3 id="sync-a-directory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Unique identifier for the Directory.|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "status": "queued"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": "directory_sync_rate_limited",
  "message": "Request could not be processed.",
  "retry_after_seconds": 120
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="sync-a-directory-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted||[DirectorySyncResponse](#schemadirectorysyncresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|409|Conflict|A sync is already in progress. No additional sync was queued.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The directory provider or state does not support manual sync.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|429|Too Many Requests|The directory is within the manual-sync cooldown window.|[DirectorySyncRateLimitError](#schemadirectorysyncratelimiterror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Directory syncing is temporarily paused. No sync was queued.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Seconds to wait before requesting another manual sync.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

<h1 id="workos-events">events</h1>

## List events

<a id="opIdEventsController_list"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/events?events=dsync.user.created%2Cdsync.user.updated' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events`

List events for the current environment. Events are returned oldest first; use `after` to page forward.

<h3 id="list-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|events|query|[string]|true|Filter events by one or more event types (e.g. `dsync.user.created`).|
|range_start|query|string(date-time)|false|ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with a `Z` suffix to filter events created after this date. Timezone offsets such as `+00:00` are not accepted.|
|range_end|query|string(date-time)|false|ISO 8601 UTC timestamp with a `Z` suffix to filter events created before this date. Timezone offsets such as `+00:00` are not accepted.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|Filter events by the [Organization](/reference/organization) that the event is associated with.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "object": "list",
  "data": [

      "object": "event",
```


`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/groups`

Get a paginated list of groups within an organization.

<h3 id="list-groups-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|The ID of the organization.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|search|query|string|false|Search groups by name or by group ID.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
  }
}
```

|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

## Update Group members

<a id="opIdGroupMembershipsController_updateMembers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY/groups/group_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/organization-memberships \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "add": [
      "om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ"
    ],
    "remove": [
      "om_01HXYZ987654321ABCDEFGHIJ"
    ]
  }'
```

`PATCH /organizations/{organizationId}/groups/{groupId}/organization-memberships`

Adds and removes organization memberships for a group in a single atomic operation. Organization memberships not listed in `add` or `remove` are left unchanged. Adding a member that is already in the group or removing a member that isn't in the group has no effect. A membership listed in both `add` and `remove` is rejected. `add` and `remove` must contain between 1 and 100 entries combined.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "add": [
    "om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ"
  ],
  "remove": [
    "om_01HXYZ987654321ABCDEFGHIJ"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-group-members-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the Organization.|
|groupId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the Group.|
|body|body|[PatchGroupMembershipsDto](#schemapatchgroupmembershipsdto)|true|none|
|» add|body|[string]|false|The IDs of the organization memberships to add to the group. Adding a membership that's already in the group has no effect.|
|» remove|body|[string]|false|The IDs of the organization memberships to remove from the group. Removing a membership that isn't in the group has no effect.|

> Example responses

```json
  "code": "action_denied",

}
```

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## List Organizations

<a id="opIdOrganizationsController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations`

Get a list of all of your existing organizations matching the criteria specified.

<h3 id="list-organizations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|domains|query|[string]|false|The domains of an Organization. Any Organization with a matching domain will be returned.|
|search|query|string|false|Searchable text for an Organization. Matches against the organization name.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "organization",
      "id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
      "name": "Acme Inc.",
      "domains": [
        {
          "object": "organization_domain",
          "id": "org_domain_01EHZNVPK2QXHMVWCEDQEKY69A",
          "organization_id": "org_01HE8GSH8FQPASKSY27THRKRBP",
          "domain": "foo-corp.com",
          "state": "pending",
          "verification_prefix": "superapp-domain-verification-z3kjny",
          "verification_token": "m5Oztg3jdK4NJLgs8uIlIprMw",
          "verification_strategy": "dns",
          "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
          "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
        }
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "tier": "diamond"
      },
      "external_id": "2fe01467-f7ea-4dd2-8b79-c2b4f56d0191",
      "stripe_customer_id": "cus_R9qWAGMQ6nGE7V",
      "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",

    }
  ],
  "list_metadata": {
    "before": "org_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "after": "org_01HXYZ987654321KJIHGFEDCBA"
  }
}
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/api_keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/api_keys`

Get a list of all API keys for an organization.

<h3 id="list-api-keys-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the Organization.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "object": "api_key",
      "id": "api_key_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
      "owner": {
        "type": "organization",
        "id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
      },
      "name": "Production API Key",
      "obfuscated_value": "sk_...3456",
      "last_used_at": null,
      "expires_at": null,
      "permissions": [
        "posts:read",
        "posts:write"
      ],
      "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ],
  "list_metadata": {
    "before": "api_key_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "after": "api_key_01HXYZ987654321KJIHGFEDCBA"
  }
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="list-api-keys-for-an-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[OrganizationApiKeyList](#schemaorganizationapikeylist)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Create an API key for an organization

<a id="opIdOrganizationApiKeysController_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/api_keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Production API Key",
    "permissions": [
      "posts:read",
      "posts:write"
    ],
    "expires_at": "2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/api_keys`

Create a new API key for an organization.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Production API Key",
  "permissions": [
    "posts:read",
    "posts:write"
  ],
  "expires_at": "2030-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-api-key-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the Organization.|
|body|body|[CreateOrganizationApiKeyDto](#schemacreateorganizationapikeydto)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the API key.|
|» permissions|body|[string]|false|The permission slugs to assign to the API key.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp when the API key should expire. Must be a future timestamp. If omitted, the key does not expire.|

```json
  "obfuscated_value": "sk_...3456",
```

<h1 id="workos-organizationsauthorized-applications">organizations.authorized-applications</h1>

Manage authorized applications for organizations.

## List authorized applications

<a id="opIdOrganizationAuthorizedApplicationsController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/authorized_applications \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/authorized_applications`

Get a list of all Connect applications that users in the organization have authorized.

<h3 id="list-authorized-applications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|The ID of the organization.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
          {
```

<h1 id="workos-organizationsdata-providers">organizations.data-providers</h1>

Manage organization-owned data providers and connected accounts.

## Get an organization connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsOrganizationController_getOrganizationDataInstallation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Retrieves an organization's [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) for a specific provider.

<h3 id="get-an-organization-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|supports_multiple_connections|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use the plural connection contract. When omitted or `false`, only the compatibility connection is considered.|
|connected_account_id|query|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select a specific connection when the organization has several for this provider.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "connected_account",
  "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "user_id": null,
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_role": "compatibility",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "user:email"
  ],
  "auth_method": "oauth",
  "api_key_last_4": null,
  "config": {},
  "state": "connected",
  "established_by_user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "state_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-organization-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The connected account was retrieved successfully.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|
|400|Bad Request|The connected account selector is malformed.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is missing a valid API key.|None|
|404|Not Found|The organization or connected account was not found.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|409|Conflict|Several connected accounts match this organization for the provider; one must be named.|[AccountSelectionRequiredErrorBody](#schemaaccountselectionrequirederrorbody)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer

## Update an organization connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsOrganizationController_updateOrganizationDataInstallation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
    "access_token": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
    "refresh_token": "ghr_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
    "scopes": [
      "repo",
      "user:email"
    ],
    "state": "connected",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Updates an organization's [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) tokens, scopes, or state for a specific provider.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "access_token": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
  "refresh_token": "ghr_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "user:email"
  ],
  "state": "connected",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organization-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|supports_multiple_connections|query|boolean|false|Accepted for compatibility; does not change update targeting. Omit intent and selector to update the compatibility connection, or supply `connected_account_id` to update an exact connection.|
|connected_account_id|query|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select the connection to update.|
|connection_intent|query|string|false|Set to `reauthorize` with `connected_account_id` to update one exact connection. The intent may be omitted when supplying an ID. Omit both for permanent compatibility behavior.|
|body|body|[OrganizationConnectedAccountDto](#schemaorganizationconnectedaccountdto)|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique connection label; null clears it. Not an account identifier.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested account identifier; null clears it.|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The OAuth access token for the connected account.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The OAuth refresh token for the connected account.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO-8601 timestamp when the access token expires. Required when `access_token` is provided for tokens that expire.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The OAuth scopes granted for this connection.|
|» state|body|string|false|Explicitly set the state of the connected account. When omitted, the state is derived from the token combination provided.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier of the organization member on whose behalf the connected account is being imported or updated. The user must be an active member of the organization.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|connected|
|» state|needs_reauthorization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "connected_account",
  "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "user_id": null,
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_role": "compatibility",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "scopes": [
    "repo",

  ],
  "auth_method": "oauth",
  "api_key_last_4": null,
  "config": {},

  "established_by_user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "state_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

```json
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "action_denied",
      "message": "Request could not be processed."
    }
  ]
}
```
