<h3 id="update-an-organization-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The connected account was updated successfully.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Imports an organization-owned [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) by providing OAuth tokens directly. Omit `connection_intent` to create only the compatibility connection, or set it to `add` to explicitly create another connection. This creation-only endpoint does not accept `connected_account_id` or reauthorization intent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "access_token": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
  "refresh_token": "ghr_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "user:email"
  ],
  "state": "connected",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_intent": "add"
}
```

<h3 id="import-an-organization-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|Makes retries of this explicit add return the connection the first attempt created instead of creating another. Reuse the same key for every retry of one request. A matching retry within 24 hours returns the existing connection; reusing the key for a different owner, integration, or authentication method, or after 24 hours while that connection exists, returns 409 `idempotency_key_conflict`. If that connection was deleted, the key creates a new one. Requests without a key are not retry-safe.|
|body|body|[CreateOrganizationConnectedAccountDto](#schemacreateorganizationconnectedaccountdto)|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique connection label; null clears it. Not an account identifier.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested account identifier; null clears it.|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The OAuth access token for the connected account.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The OAuth refresh token for the connected account.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO-8601 timestamp when the access token expires. Required when `access_token` is provided for tokens that expire.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The OAuth scopes granted for this connection.|
|» state|body|string|false|Explicitly set the state of the connected account. When omitted, the state is derived from the token combination provided.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier of the organization member on whose behalf the connected account is being imported or updated. The user must be an active member of the organization.|
|» connection_intent|body|string|false|Set to `add` to create another connected account. Omit this field for permanent compatibility behavior.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|connected|
|» state|needs_reauthorization|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "object": "connected_account",
  "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "user_id": null,
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_role": "compatibility",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",

  "established_by_user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "state_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
```

<h3 id="import-an-organization-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The connected account was created successfully.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is missing a valid API key.|None|
|403|Forbidden|The `user_id` is not an active member of the organization.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|The organization, user, or data integration was not found, or `multiple_connections_unavailable` when `connection_intent: add` would create an additional connection while additional connections are turned off for the team.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|The compatibility connection already exists for this organization and integration, `connected_account_limit_reached` when `connection_intent: add` would create a standard connection and the owner already has 25 connections, or `idempotency_key_conflict` when the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different connection request or its replay window has passed.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request body is malformed (`invalid_request_parameters`), the data integration is not in a valid state (`invalid_data_integration_state`), the token combination is invalid (`invalid_token_combination`), or no client credentials are configured for the data integration (`client_credentials_not_configured`).|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Another connection is being created for this owner and provider. Retry the request.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

<h3 id="import-an-organization-connected-account-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **404**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[ConnectionCreationNotFoundErrorBody](#schemaconnectioncreationnotfounderrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|false|none|none|

Status Code **409**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[ConnectionCreationConflictErrorBody](#schemaconnectioncreationconflicterrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|false|none|none|

Status Code **422**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[OrganizationConnectedAccountImportErrorBody](#schemaorganizationconnectedaccountimporterrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[InvalidRequestParametersErrorBodyWithErrors](#schemainvalidrequestparameterserrorbodywitherrors)|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

## Delete an organization connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsOrganizationController_deleteOrganizationDataInstallation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Disconnects the organization's account for the provider, including removing any stored access and refresh tokens. A member will need to reauthorize if the organization wants to reconnect. This does not revoke access on the provider side.

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|path|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|supports_multiple_connections|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use the plural connection contract. When omitted or `false`, only the compatibility connection is considered.|
|connected_account_id|query|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select the connection to delete.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="delete-an-organization-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|The connected account was deleted successfully.|None|
|400|Bad Request|The connected account selector is malformed.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is missing a valid API key.|None|
|404|Not Found|The organization or connected account was not found.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|409|Conflict|Several connected accounts match this organization for the provider; one must be named.|[AccountSelectionRequiredErrorBody](#schemaaccountselectionrequirederrorbody)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The connected account or its WorkOS OAuth grant is being changed by another request. Retry the request.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>


`GET /authorization/permissions`

Get a list of all permissions in your WorkOS environment.

<h3 id="list-permissions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "data": [
    {
      "object": "permission",
      "id": "perm_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",

      "system": false,
```

## List data integrations

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsManagementController_listDataIntegrations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /data-integrations`

Lists the environment's data integrations configured with `custom` or `organization` credentials, including custom providers and API key integrations. Both user-owned and organization-owned roots are returned, each as its own row with an `ownership`; filter with `ownership` to return only one kind.

<h3 id="list-data-integrations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|
|ownership|query|string|false|Only return Data Integrations with this ownership: `user` for the integrations users connect their own accounts to, or `organization` for the roots organizations connect to. Omit to return both.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|
|ownership|user|
|ownership|organization|

## Create a data integration

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsManagementController_createDataIntegration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "github",
    "ownership": "user",
    "description": "Production GitHub app",
    "enabled": true,
    "scopes": [
      "repo",
      "read:org"
    ],
    "auth_methods": [
      "oauth"
    ],
    "config": {
      "account": "myorg-myaccount"
    },
    "credentials": {
      "type": "custom",
      "client_id": "Iv1.abc123",
      "client_secret": "secret_…"
    },
    "api_key": {
      "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
      "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
      "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
    },
    "custom_provider": {
      "name": "My OAuth App",
      "authorization_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/authorize",
      "token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
      "refresh_token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
      "pkce_enabled": true,
      "request_scope_separator": " ",
      "scopes_required": false,
      "client_secret_required": true,
      "additional_authorization_parameters": {
        "prompt": "consent"
      },
      "token_body_content_type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
      "authenticate_via": "request_body"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations`

Creates a data integration for a provider. Set `credentials.type` to `custom` to use your own OAuth app credentials or `organization` to have each organization supply its own. Set `auth_methods` to `["api_key"]` to create an API key integration; you may optionally supply an `api_key` block to install a first tenant in the same call. Set `auth_methods` to `["client_credentials"]` to create a client-credentials integration; client credentials are installed per-tenant afterwards. Set `ownership` to `organization` to create the integration organizations connect to instead of the default user-owned one; a provider may have one of each. For a built-in provider, pass its slug as `provider`. For a custom provider, pass a new slug plus a `custom_provider` definition, or the slug of an existing custom provider (without `custom_provider`) to add the other ownership.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "github",
  "ownership": "user",
  "description": "Production GitHub app",
  "enabled": true,
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "read:org"
  ],
  "auth_methods": [
    "oauth"
  ],
  "config": {
    "account": "myorg-myaccount"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "type": "custom",
    "client_id": "Iv1.abc123",
    "client_secret": "secret_…"
  },
  "api_key": {
    "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  },
  "custom_provider": {
    "name": "My OAuth App",
    "authorization_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/authorize",
    "token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
    "refresh_token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
    "pkce_enabled": true,
    "request_scope_separator": " ",
    "scopes_required": false,
    "client_secret_required": true,
    "additional_authorization_parameters": {
      "prompt": "consent"
    },
    "token_body_content_type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    "authenticate_via": "request_body"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-data-integration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateDataIntegrationDto](#schemacreatedataintegrationdto)|true|none|
|» provider|body|string|true|The provider to create a Data Integration for. For a built-in provider use its slug (e.g. `github`, `slack`). For a custom provider, this is the new provider slug and `custom_provider` must be supplied. A custom provider slug cannot shadow an existing global provider slug.|
|» ownership|body|string|false|Who owns the Data Integration. `user` (the default) creates the integration users connect their own accounts to; `organization` creates the root organizations connect to. Ownership is fixed at creation, and one integration of each ownership may exist per provider. Independent of `credentials.type`.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|An optional description of the Data Integration.|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the Data Integration is enabled. Defaults to `false`.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The OAuth scopes to request for the Data Integration. Defaults to the provider's configured scopes when omitted.|
|» auth_methods|body|[string]|false|How accounts authenticate with the provider. Defaults to `["oauth"]`. Use `["api_key"]` to declare an API key integration; `credentials` is then not required and keys are supplied per-tenant (optionally via `api_key` on this request). Use `["client_credentials"]` to declare a client-credentials integration; `credentials` is likewise not required and client credentials are supplied per-tenant.|
|» config|body|object|false|Provider-specific config values (e.g. a Snowflake `account`), keyed by the config field. Only fields the built-in provider declares are accepted.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» credentials|body|[DataIntegrationCredentialsDto](#schemadataintegrationcredentialsdto)|false|The OAuth credentials to configure for the Data Integration. Required for OAuth integrations; omit when `auth_methods` is `["api_key"]`.|
|» api_key|body|[ApiKeyInstallationDto](#schemaapikeyinstallationdto)|false|An optional API key to install for the first tenant on an `api_key` integration. Omit to declare a keyless integration; tenants can be added later via the per-installation API key path.|
|» custom_provider|body|[CustomProviderDefinitionDto](#schemacustomproviderdefinitiondto)|false|The OAuth definition for a custom provider. Supply this to define a custom provider; omit it to create an integration for a built-in provider.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» ownership|user|
|» ownership|organization|
|» auth_methods|oauth|
|» auth_methods|api_key|
|» auth_methods|client_credentials|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "object": "data_integration",
  "id": "data_integration_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "slug": "github",
```

## Finish connection

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_finishConnection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/finish \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "connect_code": "Q3n0bWh2b0tqZ1VtV2ZsYkJ3cE9aV0J6T1hGb1lYaGo",
    "code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk",
    "state": "q2czJKmVAraSBg8xFpT7M9uR"
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations/finish`

Saves a connection that was started with `code_challenge`. After the user authorizes, WorkOS redirects them to `return_to` with a `connect_code` and `state`. Call this endpoint from your server with that `connect_code` and the `code_verifier` behind the challenge to save the connected account.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "connect_code": "Q3n0bWh2b0tqZ1VtV2ZsYkJ3cE9aV0J6T1hGb1lYaGo",
  "code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk",
  "state": "q2czJKmVAraSBg8xFpT7M9uR"
}
```

<h3 id="finish-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» connect_code|body|string|true|The `connect_code` WorkOS added to `return_to` when the user finished authorizing. It can be used once and expires 90 seconds after the redirect.|
|» code_verifier|body|string|true|The code verifier `code_challenge` was derived from: 43 to 128 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, `.`, `_` and `~`. A wrong verifier uses up the `connect_code`, and the user has to connect again.|
|» state|body|string|false|The `state` WorkOS added to `return_to` alongside `connect_code`. Optional; it is only used to correlate the request in logs.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "connected_account": {
    "object": "connected_account",
    "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_role": "compatibility",
    "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": null,
    "scopes": [
      "repo",
      "user:email"
    ],
    "auth_method": "oauth",
    "api_key_last_4": null,
    "config": {},
    "state": "connected",
    "established_by_user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "state_reason": null,
    "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
    "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_connect_code",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="finish-connection-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[DataIntegrationFinishConnectionResponse](#schemadataintegrationfinishconnectionresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The connection could not be completed, and the user must connect again. `invalid_connect_code` when the `connect_code` is unknown, expired, already used, or from another environment, or the `code_verifier` does not match the `code_challenge`. Other codes report why saving the connection failed, such as `target_deleted` when the connected account being reauthorized was deleted in the meantime. A malformed request body returns validation messages instead.|Inline|

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

## Upsert an API key for a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_upsertApiKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/github/api-key \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
    "connection_intent": "reauthorize",
    "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  }'
```

`PUT /data-integrations/{slug}/api-key`

Creates or updates an API-key-based installation for the specified integration, owned by the user or, when `connection_owner` is `organization`, shared by the organization. If an installation already exists, the stored API key is rotated to the new value. To create another connection, use POST.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
  "connection_intent": "reauthorize",
  "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
}
```

<h3 id="upsert-an-api-key-for-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique label. Omit to preserve an existing label; null clears it. Labels are never account identifiers.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested provider account identifier, never inferred from a label or credential. Omit to preserve an existing identifier; null clears it.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Whose connection to create or rotate. `user` (the default) addresses the connection owned by `user_id`. `organization` addresses the connection shared by every member of `organization_id`; `user_id` then identifies the member performing the request and must be an active member of the organization.|
|» secret|body|string|true|The API key secret to store for this integration.|
|» connection_intent|body|string|false|Send `reauthorize` with `connected_account_id` to reauthorize one exact connection. Omit it to use the compatibility connection; creating another connection lives on the POST route.|
|» connected_account_id|body|string|false|The exact connected account to reauthorize. Required with `connection_intent: reauthorize`; it may also be sent on its own to reauthorize that connection.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "object": "connected_account",
  "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_role": "compatibility",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "scopes": [],
  "auth_method": "api_key",
  "api_key_last_4": "cdef",
  "state": "connected",
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "entity_not_found",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "auth_method_mismatch",
  "message": "This installation uses oauth authentication. Use the POST /:slug/token endpoint instead."
}
```

<h3 id="upsert-an-api-key-for-a-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|The resulting connected account after the upsert.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[ErrorBodyWithMessageOrMessageList](#schemaerrorbodywithmessageormessagelist)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|The data integration or selected connected account was not found (`entity_not_found`).|Inline|

|422|Unprocessable Entity|The matched installation uses a different auth method than this endpoint expects.|[AuthMethodMismatchErrorBody](#schemaauthmethodmismatcherrorbody)|

## Create another API key connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_createApiKeyConnection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/github/api-key \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
    "connection_intent": "add"
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations/{slug}/api-key`

Creates another API key-based connected account for the specified integration, owned by the user or, when `connection_owner` is `organization`, shared by the organization. Requires `connection_intent: add` and does not accept `connected_account_id`; use PUT to create or rotate the compatibility connection or to update an exact connection.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
  "connection_intent": "add"
}
```

<h3 id="create-another-api-key-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|Makes retries of this explicit add return the connection the first attempt created instead of creating another. Reuse the same key for every retry of one request. A matching retry within 24 hours returns the existing connection; reusing the key for a different owner, integration, or authentication method, or after 24 hours while that connection exists, returns 409 `idempotency_key_conflict`. If that connection was deleted, the key creates a new one. Requests without a key are not retry-safe.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique label. Omit to preserve an existing label; null clears it. Labels are never account identifiers.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested provider account identifier, never inferred from a label or credential. Omit to preserve an existing identifier; null clears it.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Whose connection to create or rotate. `user` (the default) addresses the connection owned by `user_id`. `organization` addresses the connection shared by every member of `organization_id`; `user_id` then identifies the member performing the request and must be an active member of the organization.|
|» secret|body|string|true|The API key secret to store for this integration.|
|» connection_intent|body|string|true|Must be `add`: this endpoint only creates another connection. The first connection for an owner shape fills the compatibility slot; later connections are standard.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "object": "connected_account",
  "id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_role": "standard",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "scopes": [],
  "auth_method": "api_key",
  "api_key_last_4": "cdef",
  "state": "connected",
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "multiple_connections_unavailable",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "connected_account_limit_reached",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="create-another-api-key-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The connected account that was created.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|
|400|Bad Request|The request is invalid, including a missing `connection_intent: add` or a supplied `connected_account_id`.|[ErrorBodyWithMessageOrMessageList](#schemaerrorbodywithmessageormessagelist)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|The data integration was not found, or `multiple_connections_unavailable` when additional connections are turned off for the team.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|`connected_account_limit_reached` when the provider and owner already have 25 connections, or `idempotency_key_conflict` when the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different connection request or its replay window has passed.|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Another connection is being created for this owner and provider. Retry the request.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

## Get authorization URL

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_getDataIntegrationAuthorizeUrl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/github/authorize \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "return_to": "https://example.com/callback",
    "code_challenge": "E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM",
    "code_challenge_method": "S256",
    "config": {
      "subdomain": "acme"
    },
    "connection_intent": "add",
    "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations/{slug}/authorize`

Generates an OAuth authorization URL to initiate the connection flow for a user. Redirect the user to the returned URL to begin the OAuth flow with the third-party provider.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "return_to": "https://example.com/callback",
  "code_challenge": "E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM",
  "code_challenge_method": "S256",
  "config": {
    "subdomain": "acme"
  },
  "connection_intent": "add",
  "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
}
```

<h3 id="get-authorization-url-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique label. Omit to preserve an existing label; null clears it. Labels are never account identifiers.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user to authorize. When `connection_owner` is `organization`, this is the user authorizing on behalf of the organization; they must be an active member of the organization and do not become the owner of the resulting connected account.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An organization ID to scope the authorization to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Who will own the connected account. `user` (the default) connects the user's own account. `organization` connects the organization's shared account and requires `organization_id`.|
|» return_to|body|string(uri)|false|The URL to redirect the user to after authorization. Required with `code_challenge`, and must then exactly match a redirect URI registered on one of the environment's applications. Loopback URLs match on any port; wildcard redirect URIs are not honored, and a `return_to` with a query string or fragment never matches.|
|» code_challenge|body|string|false|A PKCE-style code challenge: the base64url-encoded SHA-256 of a `code_verifier` your app keeps. When set, the connection isn't saved when the user finishes authorizing. Instead, the user is redirected to `return_to` with a `connect_code` and `state`, and your app must call [Finish connection](/reference/pipes/connected-account/finish-connection) with the `connect_code` and `code_verifier` within 90 seconds to save it.|
|» code_challenge_method|body|string|false|The method used to derive `code_challenge`. Only `S256` is supported, and it is the default. Requires `code_challenge`.|
|» config|body|object|false|Connect-time config values for the provider-declared `installation`-scope fields (e.g. a Zendesk `subdomain`), keyed by the config field. Only fields the provider declares may be supplied, and required fields must be provided unless already pinned on the integration.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» connection_intent|body|string|false|Which connection the request targets. Omit it to use the compatibility connection. Send `add` to create another connection: the first connection for an owner shape fills the compatibility slot, and later connections are standard. Send `reauthorize` with `connected_account_id` to reauthorize one exact connection.|
|» connected_account_id|body|string|false|The exact connected account to reauthorize. Required with `connection_intent: reauthorize` and not accepted otherwise.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|
|» connection_intent|add|
|» connection_intent|reauthorize|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "url": "https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/q2czJKmVAraSBg8xFpT7M9uR/authorize-redirect",
  "state": "01K8ZQ6Y3J4N5P7R9T2V4W6X8Z",
  "completion": "finish_required"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_return_to",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": "multiple_connections_unavailable",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "connected_account_limit_reached",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "auth_method_mismatch",
  "message": "This installation uses oauth authentication. Use the POST /:slug/token endpoint instead."
}
```

<h3 id="get-authorization-url-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[DataIntegrationAuthorizeUrlResponse](#schemadataintegrationauthorizeurlresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|The request was invalid. With `code_challenge`: `invalid_return_to` when `return_to` is missing or does not exactly match a registered redirect URI, `return_to_requires_exact_match` when only a wildcard redirect URI matches it, and `connect_finish_unavailable` when `code_challenge` is not available for the environment.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|The integration or user was not found (`entity_not_found`); `connected_account_not_found` when `connected_account_id` does not name a connection for this owner and integration; or `multiple_connections_unavailable` when `connection_intent: add` would create an additional connection while additional connections are turned off for the team.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|`connected_account_limit_reached` when explicit add would create a standard connection for a provider and owner that already has 25 connections.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The selected connected account does not use OAuth authentication.|[AuthMethodMismatchError](#schemaauthmethodmismatcherror)|

## Upsert client credentials for a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_upsertClientCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/salesforce/client-credentials \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "account_display_name": "Acme production",
    "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "client_id": "3MVG9...",
    "client_secret": "shhh-secret",
    "config": {
      "salesforce_host": "acme.my.salesforce.com"
    },
    "connection_intent": "reauthorize",
    "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  }'
```

`PUT /data-integrations/{slug}/client-credentials`

Creates or updates a client-credentials-based installation for the specified integration, owned by the user or, when `connection_owner` is `organization`, shared by the organization. If an installation already exists, the stored client credentials are rotated to the new values. To create another connection, use POST.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "client_id": "3MVG9...",
  "client_secret": "shhh-secret",
  "config": {
    "salesforce_host": "acme.my.salesforce.com"
  },
  "connection_intent": "reauthorize",
  "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
}
```

<h3 id="upsert-client-credentials-for-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique label. Omit to preserve an existing label; null clears it. Labels are never account identifiers.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested provider account identifier, never inferred from a label or credential. Omit to preserve an existing identifier; null clears it.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Whose connection to create or rotate. `user` (the default) addresses the connection owned by `user_id`. `organization` addresses the connection shared by every member of `organization_id`; `user_id` then identifies the member performing the request and must be an active member of the organization.|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The OAuth client ID to store for this integration.|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The OAuth client secret to store for this integration.|
|» config|body|object|false|Provider-specific configuration values collected for this installation, keyed by the provider's config field descriptors.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» connection_intent|body|string|false|Send `reauthorize` with `connected_account_id` to reauthorize one exact connection. Omit it to use the compatibility connection; creating another connection lives on the POST route.|
|» connected_account_id|body|string|false|The exact connected account to reauthorize. Required with `connection_intent: reauthorize`; it may also be sent on its own to reauthorize that connection.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|

`POST /data-integrations/{slug}/client-credentials`

Creates another client credentials-based connected account for the specified integration, owned by the user or, when `connection_owner` is `organization`, shared by the organization. Requires `connection_intent: add` and does not accept `connected_account_id`; use PUT to create or rotate the compatibility connection or to update an exact connection.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "client_id": "3MVG9...",
  "client_secret": "shhh-secret",
  "config": {
    "salesforce_host": "acme.my.salesforce.com"
  },
  "connection_intent": "add"
}
```

<h3 id="create-another-client-credentials-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|Makes retries of this explicit add return the connection the first attempt created instead of creating another. Reuse the same key for every retry of one request. A matching retry within 24 hours returns the existing connection; reusing the key for a different owner, integration, or authentication method, or after 24 hours while that connection exists, returns 409 `idempotency_key_conflict`. If that connection was deleted, the key creates a new one. Requests without a key are not retry-safe.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique label. Omit to preserve an existing label; null clears it. Labels are never account identifiers.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested provider account identifier, never inferred from a label or credential. Omit to preserve an existing identifier; null clears it.|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Whose connection to create or rotate. `user` (the default) addresses the connection owned by `user_id`. `organization` addresses the connection shared by every member of `organization_id`; `user_id` then identifies the member performing the request and must be an active member of the organization.|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The OAuth client ID to store for this integration.|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The OAuth client secret to store for this integration.|
|» config|body|object|false|Provider-specific configuration values collected for this installation, keyed by the provider's config field descriptors.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» connection_intent|body|string|true|Must be `add`: this endpoint only creates another connection. The first connection for an owner shape fills the compatibility slot; later connections are standard.|

|» connection_owner|organization|

## Vend credentials for a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_vendCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/github/credentials \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "supports_multiple_connections": true
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations/{slug}/credentials`

Returns credentials for a user's connected account. Branches on the installation's `auth_method`: OAuth installations return an access token (refreshed if needed); API-key installations return the stored secret. Every active credential includes `config`: provider-declared, non-secret values from the installation snapshot, with current provider defaults for unset fields. Editing integration or organization configuration does not change the snapshot; reconnect or explicitly rebind the connection to adopt those edits. Defaults remain live, so a changed default can appear in `config` before a cached token is refreshed or re-minted. Credentials that never refresh require a reconnect or rebind when a default changes their routing.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "supports_multiple_connections": true
}
```

<h3 id="vend-credentials-for-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier. When `connection_owner` is `organization`, this is the user the credentials are vended on behalf of; they must be an active member of the organization.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connected_account_id|body|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select a specific connection when the user has several for this provider.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Which connection to vend from. `user` (the default) vends the user's own connection and requires `user_id`. `organization` vends the organization's shared connection and requires `organization_id`.|
|» supports_multiple_connections|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use the plural connection contract. If no `connected_account_id` is supplied and several connections match, the request returns `account_selection_required`. When omitted or `false`, only the compatibility connection is considered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "credential": {
    "object": "credential",
    "auth_method": "oauth",
    "value": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
    "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",

    ],

    "config": {}
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

For custom providers, `custom_provider` updates the OAuth definition, which is shared with the user-owned root. ## Get an access token for a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsController_getUserlandUserToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/data-integrations/github/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "connection_owner": "user",
    "supports_multiple_connections": true
  }'
```

`POST /data-integrations/{slug}/token`

Fetches a valid OAuth access token for a user's connected account. WorkOS automatically handles token refresh, ensuring you always receive a valid, non-expired token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connected_account_id": "data_installation_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "connection_owner": "user",
  "supports_multiple_connections": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-access-token-for-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|slug|path|string|true|The identifier of the integration.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier. When `connection_owner` is `organization`, this is the user the credentials are vended on behalf of; they must be an active member of the organization.|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter to scope the connection to a specific organization. Required when `connection_owner` is `organization`.|
|» connected_account_id|body|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select a specific connection when the user has several for this provider.|
|» connection_owner|body|string|false|Which connection to vend from. `user` (the default) vends the user's own connection and requires `user_id`. `organization` vends the organization's shared connection and requires `organization_id`.|
|» supports_multiple_connections|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use the plural connection contract. If no `connected_account_id` is supplied and several connections match, the request returns `account_selection_required`. When omitted or `false`, only the compatibility connection is considered.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» connection_owner|user|
|» connection_owner|organization|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "access_token": {
    "object": "access_token",
    "access_token": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
    "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
    "scopes": [
      "repo",
      "user:email"
    ],
    "missing_scopes": []
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "auth_method_mismatch",
  "message": "This installation uses oauth authentication. Use the POST /:slug/token endpoint instead."
}
```

<h3 id="get-an-access-token-for-a-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[DataIntegrationAccessTokenResponse](#schemadataintegrationaccesstokenresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|The user is not an active member of the organization named for an organization connection or an organization-scoped personal connection.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|404|Not Found|The data integration or selected connected account was not found.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|409|Conflict|Several connected accounts match this user or organization for the provider; one must be named.|[AccountSelectionRequiredError](#schemaaccountselectionrequirederror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The matched installation uses a different auth method than this endpoint expects.|[AuthMethodMismatchError](#schemaauthmethodmismatcherror)|

## Configure a provider for an organization

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/organizations/org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/data_integration_configurations/github \
```

`PUT /organizations/{organizationId}/data_integration_configurations/{slug}`

Creates or updates an organization's provider configuration. Use this endpoint to enable or disable a provider, set custom OAuth scopes, or supply organization-managed OAuth credentials.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "user:email"
  ],
  "client_id": "client_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "client_secret": "••••••••",
  "config": {
    "account": "myorg-myaccount"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="configure-a-provider-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organizationId|path|string|true|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier to configure the provider for.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider to configure (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|body|body|[ConfigureDataIntegrationBody](#schemaconfiguredataintegrationbody)|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|false|Whether the provider is enabled for the organization.|
|» scopes|body|[string] \| null|false|The OAuth scopes to request for the organization. Pass `null` to inherit the provider scopes.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|null|false|none|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The OAuth client ID of the organization's own application. Must be provided together with `client_secret`, and only for providers whose credentials are supplied by the organization.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The OAuth client secret of the organization's own application. Must be provided together with `client_id`.|
|» config|body|object|false|Provider-specific config values to set for the organization, keyed by config field. Only fields the provider declares are accepted, and each value must match that field's pattern. Accepted only for providers whose credentials are organization-managed; for shared or custom credential providers, config belongs on the integration itself (via the data-integrations API) and supplying it here is rejected.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

Creates a team along with its default project, a staging environment, and a production environment. An admin invitation is sent to `admin_email`, onboarding is marked complete with AuthKit enabled, and the calling platform is authorized to act inside the team.

```json
  "admin_email": "alice@example.com",
  "name": "Example Team"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Create an attempt

<a id="opIdRadarStandaloneController_assess"></a>

```bash
    "auth_method": "Password",
    "action": "sign-in",

  }'
```

`POST /radar/attempts`

Assess a request for risk using the Radar engine and receive a verdict.

```json
  "ip_address": "49.78.240.97",
```

<h1 id="workos-sso">sso</h1>

Single Sign-On endpoints.

## Initiate SSO

<a id="opIdSsoController_authorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/sso/authorize?client_id=client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fcallback&response_type=code' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /sso/authorize`

Initiates the single sign-on flow.

<h3 id="initiate-sso-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider_scopes|query|[string]|false|Additional scopes to request from the identity provider. Applicable when using OAuth or OpenID Connect connections.|
|provider_query_params|query|object|false|Key/value pairs of query parameters to pass to the OAuth provider. Only applicable when using OAuth connections.|
|client_id|query|string|true|The unique identifier of the WorkOS environment client.|
|domain|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Use `connection` or `organization` instead. Used to initiate SSO for a connection by domain. The domain must be associated with a connection in your WorkOS environment.|
|provider|query|string|false|Used to initiate OAuth authentication with various providers.|
|redirect_uri|query|string(uri)|true|Where to redirect the user after they complete the authentication process. You must use one of the redirect URIs configured via the [Redirects](https://dashboard.workos.com/redirects) page on the dashboard.|
|response_type|query|string|true|The only valid option for the response type parameter is `"code"`.<br><br>The `"code"` parameter value initiates an [authorization code grant type](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-4.1). This grant type allows you to exchange an authorization code for an access token during the redirect that takes place after a user has authenticated with an identity provider.|
|state|query|string|false|An optional parameter that can be used to encode arbitrary information to help restore application state between redirects. If included, the redirect URI received from WorkOS will contain the exact `state` that was passed.|
|connection|query|string|false|Used to initiate SSO for a connection. The value should be a WorkOS connection ID.<br><br>You can persist the WorkOS connection ID with application user or team identifiers. WorkOS will use the connection indicated by the connection parameter to direct the user to the corresponding IdP for authentication.|
|organization|query|string|false|Used to initiate SSO for an organization. The value should be a WorkOS organization ID.<br><br>You can persist the WorkOS organization ID with application user or team identifiers. WorkOS will use the organization ID to determine the appropriate connection and the IdP to direct the user to for authentication.|
|domain_hint|query|string|false|Can be used to pre-fill the domain field when initiating authentication with Microsoft OAuth or with a Google SAML connection type.|
|login_hint|query|string|false|Can be used to pre-fill the username/email address field of the IdP sign-in page for the user, if you know their username ahead of time. Currently supported for OAuth, OpenID Connect, Okta, Entra ID, and custom SAML connections.|
|nonce|query|string|false|A random string generated by the client that is used to mitigate replay attacks.|
|prompt|query|string|false|If set to `login`, forces re-authentication at the identity provider. For supported SAML providers this sets `ForceAuthn="true"` in the SAML request; providers that don't support it are unaffected.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|provider|AppleOAuth|
|provider|BitbucketOAuth|
|provider|GitHubOAuth|
|provider|GitLabOAuth|
|provider|GoogleOAuth|
|provider|IntuitOAuth|
|provider|LinkedInOAuth|
|provider|MicrosoftOAuth|
|provider|SalesforceOAuth|
|provider|SlackOAuth|
|provider|VercelMarketplaceOAuth|
|provider|VercelOAuth|
|provider|XeroOAuth|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "url": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=example&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.workos.com%2Fsso%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=openid%20profile%20email"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-sso-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[SsoAuthorizeUrlResponse](#schemassoauthorizeurlresponse)|
|302|Found||None|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|302|Location|string|uri|none|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Logout Redirect

<a id="opIdSsoController_logout"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/sso/logout?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJwcm9maWxlX2lkIjoicHJvZl8wMUdXUTFHMEgyRk02QVNFRjBIUzEzSENXOS0zMDRrZzAzZyIsImV4cCI6IjE1MTYyMzkwMjIifQ.Wru9Qlnf5DpohtGCKhZU4cVOd3zpiu7QQ-XEX--5A_4' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /sso/logout`

Logout allows to sign out a user from your application by triggering the identity provider sign out flow. This `GET` endpoint should be a redirection, since the identity provider user will be identified in the browser session.

Before redirecting to this endpoint, you need to generate a short-lived logout token using the [Logout Authorize](/reference/sso/logout/authorize) endpoint.

<h3 id="logout-redirect-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|query|string|true|The logout token returned from the [Logout Authorize](/reference/sso/logout/authorize) endpoint.|

> Example responses

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="logout-redirect-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|302|Found||None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

|302|Location|string|uri|none|

</aside>

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/sso/token?client_id=client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X&client_secret=sk_example_123456789&grant_type=authorization_code' \
  -X POST \
```

`POST /sso/token`

```json
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "code_verifier": "code_verifier_value",
  "subject_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjMifQ.example",

  "organization_id": "org_01EHQMYV6MBK39QC5PZXHY59C3"
}
```

## Authenticate

<a id="opIdUserlandSessionsController_authenticate[0]"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/authenticate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "client_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "client_secret": "sk_test_....",
    "grant_type": "authorization_code",
    "code": "vBqZKaPpsnJlPfXiDqN7b6VTz",
    "code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk",
    "invitation_token": "inv_tok_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "ip_address": "203.0.113.42",
    "device_id": "device_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0",
    "signals_id": "01JBS0GN92GC2RJQS4X9DBPQ2A"
  }'
```

## Get an authorization URL

<a id="opIdUserlandSsoController_authorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.workos.com/user_management/authorize?response_type=code&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fcallback&client_id=client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X'
```

`GET /user_management/authorize`

Generates an OAuth 2.0 authorization URL to authenticate a user with AuthKit or SSO.

<h3 id="get-an-authorization-url-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code_challenge_method|query|string|false|The only valid PKCE code challenge method is `"S256"`. Required when specifying a `code_challenge`.|
|code_challenge|query|string|false|Code challenge derived from the code verifier used for the PKCE flow.|
|domain_hint|query|string|false|A domain hint for SSO connection lookup.|
|connection_id|query|string|false|The ID of an SSO connection to use for authentication.|
|provider_query_params|query|object|false|Key/value pairs of query parameters to pass to the OAuth provider.|
|provider_scopes|query|[string]|false|Additional OAuth scopes to request from the identity provider.|
|invitation_token|query|string|false|A token representing a user invitation to redeem during authentication.|
|max_age|query|integer|false|Maximum allowable elapsed time, in seconds, since the user last actively authenticated. If the last authentication is older than this value, the user is prompted to re-authenticate; a value of `0` forces re-authentication. Only supported when the provider is `authkit`.|
|screen_hint|query|string|false|Used to specify which screen to display when the provider is `authkit`.|
|login_hint|query|string|false|A hint to the authorization server about the login identifier the user might use.|
|provider|query|string|false|The OAuth provider to authenticate with (e.g., GoogleOAuth, MicrosoftOAuth, GitHubOAuth).|
|prompt|query|string|false|Controls the authentication flow behavior for the user.|
|state|query|string|false|An opaque value used to maintain state between the request and the callback.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|The ID of the organization to authenticate the user against.|
|response_type|query|string|true|The response type of the application.|
|redirect_uri|query|string(uri)|true|The callback URI where the authorization code will be sent after authentication.|
|client_id|query|string|true|The unique identifier of the WorkOS environment client.|

|Parameter|Value|

|screen_hint|sign-in|

## Get device authorization URL

<a id="opIdUserlandSsoController_deviceAuthorization"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/authorize/device \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "client_id": "client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X"
  }'
```

`POST /user_management/authorize/device`

Initiates the CLI Auth flow by requesting a device code and verification URLs. This endpoint implements the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Flow ([RFC 8628](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628)) and is designed for command-line applications or other devices with limited input capabilities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "client_id": "client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X"
}
```

<h3 id="get-device-authorization-url-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The WorkOS client ID for your application.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "device_code": "CVE2wOfIFK4vhmiDBntpX9s8KT2f0qngpWYL0LGy9HxYgBRXUKIUkZB9BgIFho5h",
  "user_code": "BCDF-GHJK",
  "verification_uri": "https://authkit_domain/device",
  "verification_uri_complete": "https://authkit_domain/device?user_code=BCDF-GHJK",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "interval": 5
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "access_denied",
  "error_description": "The request failed due to: invitation_invalid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "access_denied",
  "error_description": "The request failed due to: invitation_invalid."
}
```

<h3 id="get-device-authorization-url-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Device authorization response with codes and verification URI.|[DeviceAuthorizationResponse](#schemadeviceauthorizationresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Invalid request parameters.|[OAuthErrorBody](#schemaoautherrorbody)|
|403|Forbidden|Feature not enabled for team.|[OAuthErrorBody](#schemaoautherrorbody)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Send a Radar SMS challenge

<a id="opIdPublicRadarChallengesController_sendRadarSmsChallenge"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/radar_challenges \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
    "pending_authentication_token": "cTDQJTTkTkkVYxbn...",
    "phone_number": "+15555550123",
    "ip_address": "203.0.113.42",
    "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  }'
```

`POST /user_management/radar_challenges`

Sends a one-time verification code over SMS to a user as part of a Radar challenge. Use the returned `verification_id` to authenticate the user with the `urn:workos:oauth:grant-type:radar-sms-challenge:code` grant type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_id": "user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "pending_authentication_token": "cTDQJTTkTkkVYxbn...",
  "phone_number": "+15555550123",
  "ip_address": "203.0.113.42",
  "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-radar-sms-challenge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SendRadarSmsChallengeDto](#schemasendradarsmschallengedto)|true|none|
|» user_id|body|string|true|The ID of the user to send the SMS challenge to.|
|» pending_authentication_token|body|string|true|The pending authentication token from a previous authentication attempt that triggered the Radar challenge.|
|» phone_number|body|string|true|The phone number to send the SMS verification code to.|
|» ip_address|body|string|false|The IP address of the user's request.|
|» user_agent|body|string|false|The user agent string from the user's request.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "verification_id": "vrf_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
  "phone_number": "+15555550123"
}
```

<h3 id="send-a-radar-sms-challenge-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[SendRadarSmsChallengeResponse](#schemasendradarsmschallengeresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

## List MCP resource indicators

<a id="opIdAuthkitOauthResourcesController_list"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

```

`GET /user_management/authkit_oauth_resources`

Lists the MCP resource indicators configured for an environment.

<h3 id="list-mcp-resource-indicators-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
    {
      "object": "authkit_oauth_resource",

      "uri": "https://api.example.com",
      "default": false,
```

`POST /user_management/authkit_oauth_resources`

Adds an MCP resource indicator (RFC 8707) to an environment, leaving any others in place.

```json
  "uri": "https://api.example.com",

}
```

|» default|body|boolean|false|Whether the resource being created becomes the environment default, clearing any previous default. Applies at creation only — this API has no update endpoint yet, so changing the default on an existing resource is done from the dashboard. A wildcard pattern cannot be the default.|

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

`PUT /user_management/users/{user_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Updates a user's [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) tokens, scopes, or state for a specific provider.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",

  "refresh_token": "ghr_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",

    "user:email"
  ],
  "state": "connected"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|organization_id|query|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter if the connection is scoped to an organization.|
|supports_multiple_connections|query|boolean|false|Accepted for compatibility; does not change update targeting. Omit intent and selector to update the compatibility connection, or supply `connected_account_id` to update an exact connection.|
|connected_account_id|query|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select the connection to update.|
|connection_intent|query|string|false|Set to `reauthorize` with `connected_account_id` to update one exact connection. The intent may be omitted when supplying an ID. Omit both for permanent compatibility behavior.|
|body|body|[ConnectedAccountDto](#schemaconnectedaccountdto)|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique connection label; null clears it. Not an account identifier.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested account identifier; null clears it.|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The OAuth access token for the connected account.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The OAuth refresh token for the connected account.|

|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The OAuth scopes granted for this connection.|
|» state|body|string|false|Explicitly set the state of the connected account. When omitted, the state is derived from the token combination provided.|

## Import a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsUserManagementController_createUserDataInstallation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/users/user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \

    "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
    "scopes": [
      "repo",
      "user:email"
    ],
    "state": "connected",
    "connection_intent": "add"
  }'
```

`POST /user_management/users/{user_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Imports a [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) for a user by providing OAuth tokens directly. Use this to migrate existing connections or set up connections without going through the OAuth flow.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "account_identifier": "workspace_123",
  "access_token": "gho_16C7e42F292c6912E7710c838347Ae178B4a",
  "refresh_token": "ghr_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "expires_at": "2025-12-31T23:59:59.000Z",
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "user:email"
  ],
  "state": "connected",
  "connection_intent": "add"
}
```

<h3 id="import-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|organization_id|query|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter if the connection is scoped to an organization.|
|idempotency-key|header|string|false|Makes retries of this explicit add return the connection the first attempt created instead of creating another. Reuse the same key for every retry of one request. A matching retry within 24 hours returns the existing connection; reusing the key for a different owner, integration, or authentication method, or after 24 hours while that connection exists, returns 409 `idempotency_key_conflict`. If that connection was deleted, the key creates a new one. Requests without a key are not retry-safe.|
|body|body|[CreateConnectedAccountDto](#schemacreateconnectedaccountdto)|true|none|
|» account_display_name|body|string \| null|false|A mutable, non-unique connection label; null clears it. Not an account identifier.|
|» account_identifier|body|string \| null|false|A developer-attested account identifier; null clears it.|
|» access_token|body|string|false|The OAuth access token for the connected account.|
|» refresh_token|body|string|false|The OAuth refresh token for the connected account.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The ISO-8601 timestamp when the access token expires. Required when `access_token` is provided for tokens that expire.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The OAuth scopes granted for this connection.|
|» state|body|string|false|Explicitly set the state of the connected account. When omitted, the state is derived from the token combination provided.|
|» connection_intent|body|string|false|Set to `add` to create another connected account. Omit this field for permanent compatibility behavior.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» state|connected|
|» state|needs_reauthorization|

```json
  "connection_role": "compatibility",
```
