```json
  "account_display_name": "Acme production",
  "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",

    "repo",

  ],
  "auth_method": "oauth",
  "api_key_last_4": null,

  "established_by_user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "state_reason": null,
  "created_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-16T14:20:00.000Z"
}
```

```json
  "code": "multiple_connections_unavailable",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

```json
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_refresh_token",

}
```

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
```

<h3 id="import-a-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The connected account was created successfully.|[ConnectedAccount](#schemaconnectedaccount)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request is missing a valid API key.|None|
|404|Not Found|The user, organization, or data integration was not found, or `multiple_connections_unavailable` when `connection_intent: add` would create an additional connection while additional connections are turned off for the team.|Inline|
|409|Conflict|The compatibility connection already exists for this user, integration, and organization, `connected_account_limit_reached` when `connection_intent: add` would create a standard connection and the owner already has 25 connections, or `idempotency_key_conflict` when the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different connection request or its replay window has passed.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request body is malformed (`invalid_request_parameters`), the data integration is not in a valid state (`invalid_data_integration_state`), the token combination is invalid (`invalid_token_combination`), no client credentials are configured for the data integration (`client_credentials_not_configured`), or `refresh_token` is not an active WorkOS OAuth grant of this user (`invalid_refresh_token`).|Inline|
|503|Service Unavailable|Another connection is being created for this owner and provider, or the WorkOS OAuth grant behind `refresh_token` is being changed. Retry the request.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

## Delete a connected account

<a id="opIdDataIntegrationsUserManagementController_deleteUserDataInstallation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/users/user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT/connected_accounts/github \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /user_management/users/{user_id}/connected_accounts/{slug}`

Disconnects WorkOS's account for the user, including removing any stored access and refresh tokens. The user will need to reauthorize if they want to reconnect. Access is not revoked on the provider side, except for the WorkOS OAuth provider, whose underlying AuthKit grant is revoked.

<h3 id="delete-a-connected-account-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|A [User](/reference/authkit/user) identifier.|
|slug|path|string|true|The slug identifier of the provider (e.g., `github`, `slack`, `notion`).|
|organization_id|query|string|false|An [Organization](/reference/organization) identifier. Optional parameter if the connection is scoped to an organization.|
|supports_multiple_connections|query|boolean|false|Set to `true` to use the plural connection contract. When omitted or `false`, only the compatibility connection is considered.|
|connected_account_id|query|string|false|A [connected account](/reference/pipes/connected-account) identifier. Use this to select the connection to delete.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "account_selection_required",
  "message": "Several connected accounts match this user for this provider. Name one with a connected account id."
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="delete-a-connected-account-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|401|Unauthorized|The request is missing a valid API key.|None|
|404|Not Found|The user, organization, or connected account was not found.|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|409|Conflict|Several connected accounts match this user for the provider; one must be named.|[AccountSelectionRequiredErrorBody](#schemaaccountselectionrequirederrorbody)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The connected account or its WorkOS OAuth grant is being changed by another request. Retry the request.|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

<h1 id="workos-user-managementinvitations">user-management.invitations</h1>

Manage user invitations.

## List invitations

<a id="opIdUserlandUserInvitesController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/invitations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user_management/invitations`

Get a list of all of invitations matching the criteria specified.

<h3 id="list-invitations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `desc`.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|The ID of the [organization](/reference/organization) that the recipient will join.|
|email|query|string(email)|false|The email address of the recipient.|

#### Enumerated Values

`POST /user_management/invitations/{id}/accept`

```json
{

}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

<h3 id="accept-an-invitation-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|string|true|none|Distinguishes the invitation object.|
|id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the invitation.|
|email|string|true|none|The email address of the recipient.|
|state|string|true|none|The state of the invitation.|
|accepted_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the invitation was accepted, or null if not yet accepted.|
|revoked_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the invitation was revoked, or null if not revoked.|
|expires_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the invitation expires.|
|organization_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the [organization](/reference/organization) that the recipient will join.|
|inviter_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who invited the recipient, if provided.|
|accepted_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who accepted the invitation, once accepted.|
|role_slug|string \| null|true|none|Slug of the role the invitee will be assigned on acceptance. Reflects the current role on the invitee's organization membership. null when the invitation has no associated organization.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|token|string|true|none|The token used to accept the invitation.|
|accept_invitation_url|string(password)|true|none|The URL where the recipient can accept the invitation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|pending|
|state|accepted|
|state|expired|
|state|revoked|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>

|organization_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the [organization](/reference/organization) that the recipient will join.|
|inviter_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who invited the recipient, if provided.|
|accepted_user_id|string \| null|true|none|The ID of the user who accepted the invitation, once accepted.|
|role_slug|string \| null|true|none|Slug of the role the invitee will be assigned on acceptance. Reflects the current role on the invitee's organization membership. null when the invitation has no associated organization.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|token|string|true|none|The token used to accept the invitation.|
|accept_invitation_url|string(password)|true|none|The URL where the recipient can accept the invitation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|pending|
|state|accepted|
|state|expired|
|state|revoked|

<h1 id="workos-user-managementmagic-auth">user-management.magic-auth</h1>

Magic auth endpoints.

## Create a Magic Auth code

<a id="opIdUserlandMagicAuthController_sendMagicAuthCodeAndReturn"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/magic_auth \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
    "invitation_token": "Z1Y2X3W4V5U6T7S8R9Q0P1O2N3",
    "ip_address": "203.0.113.42",
    "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0",
    "radar_auth_attempt_id": "radar_auth_attempt_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "signals_id": "01JBS0GN92GC2RJQS4X9DBPQ2A",
    "locale": "en"
  }'
```

`POST /user_management/magic_auth`

Creates a one-time authentication code that can be sent to the user's email address. The code expires in 10 minutes. To verify the code, [authenticate the user with Magic Auth](/reference/authkit/authentication/magic-auth).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
  "invitation_token": "Z1Y2X3W4V5U6T7S8R9Q0P1O2N3",
  "ip_address": "203.0.113.42",
  "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0",
  "radar_auth_attempt_id": "radar_auth_attempt_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
  "signals_id": "01JBS0GN92GC2RJQS4X9DBPQ2A",
  "locale": "en"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-magic-auth-code-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|body|body|[CreateUserlandMagicCodeAndReturnDto](#schemacreateuserlandmagiccodeandreturndto)|true|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address to send the magic code to.|
|» invitation_token|body|string|false|The invitation token to associate with this magic code.|
|» ip_address|body|string|false|The IP address of the user's request. Required when Radar is in Decision mode.|
|» user_agent|body|string|false|The user agent string from the user's request.|
|» radar_auth_attempt_id|body|string|false|The ID of an existing Radar authentication attempt to associate with this request.|
|» signals_id|body|string|false|An optional Radar signals ID to correlate client-side signals with this request.|
|» locale|body|string|false|The locale to use when rendering the Magic Auth email. Defaults to the environment's default locale. See [supported locales](/authkit/hosted-ui#localization).|

<h1 id="workos-user-managementorganization-membership">user-management.organization-membership</h1>

Manage user organization memberships.

## List organization memberships

<a id="opIdUserlandUserOrganizationMembershipsController_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/organization_memberships \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /user_management/organization_memberships`

Get a list of all organization memberships matching the criteria specified. At least one of `user_id` or `organization_id` must be provided. By default only active memberships are returned. Use the `statuses` parameter to filter by other statuses.

<h3 id="list-organization-memberships-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `desc`.|
|organization_id|query|string|false|The ID of the [organization](/reference/organization) which the user belongs to.|
|statuses|query|[string]|false|Filter by the status of the organization membership. Array including any of `active`, `inactive`, or `pending`.|
|user_id|query|string|false|The ID of the [user](/reference/authkit/user).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|
|statuses|active|
|statuses|inactive|
|statuses|pending|

## Deactivate an organization membership

<a id="opIdUserlandUserOrganizationMembershipsController_deactivate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/organization_memberships/om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/deactivate \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /user_management/organization_memberships/{id}/deactivate`

Deactivates an `active` organization membership. Emits an [organization_membership.updated](/events/organization-membership) event upon successful deactivation.

- Deactivating an `inactive` membership is a no-op and does not emit an event.
- Deactivating a `pending` membership returns an error. This membership should be [deleted](/reference/authkit/organization-membership/delete) instead.

See the [membership management documentation](/authkit/users-organizations/organizations/membership-management) for additional details.

## Reactivate an organization membership

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/organization_memberships/om_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ/reactivate \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /user_management/organization_memberships/{id}/reactivate`

Reactivates an `inactive` organization membership, retaining the pre-existing role(s). Emits an [organization_membership.updated](/events/organization-membership) event upon successful reactivation.

- Reactivating an `active` membership is a no-op and does not emit an event.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|omId|path|string|true|Unique identifier of the Organization Membership.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). |before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `desc`.|
|organization|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Filter users by the organization they are a member of. Deprecated in favor of `organization_id`.|

|email|query|string|false|Filter users by their email address.|

`GET /user_management/users/{id}/sessions`

Get a list of all active sessions for a specific user.

<h3 id="list-sessions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `desc`.|

`DELETE /user_management/waitlist_entries/{id}`

## Approve a waitlist entry

<a id="opIdWaitlistEntriesController_approve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/waitlist_entries/wl_user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5/approve \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /user_management/waitlist_entries/{id}/approve`

Approve a waitlist entry, create an invitation for its email address, and send the invitation email. Approving a denied entry reverses the denial. The approval is saved even when the invitation steps fail, so instead of retrying the approval, recover based on the outcome:

- `200` — the entry is approved. If invitation creation failed, no invitation exists yet; [send](/reference/authkit/invitation/send) one.
- `422` with code `invitation_email_not_sent` — the entry is approved and an invitation exists, but its email was not sent; [resend](/reference/authkit/invitation/resend) it.
- `422` with code `invalid_state` — the entry was already approved.

<h3 id="approve-a-waitlist-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the waitlist entry.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "wl_user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
  "state": "approved",
  "approved_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "additional_fields": {
    "company": "Example Corp"
  },
  "waitlist_id": "waitlist_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "object": "waitlist_entry"
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

## Create a waitlist entry

<a id="opIdWaitlistsController_createEntry"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/user_management/waitlists/default/entries \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
    "additional_fields": {
      "company": "Example Corp"
    },
    "send_confirmation_email": false
  }'
```

`POST /user_management/waitlists/{id}/entries`

Add an email address to the waitlist. Email addresses are normalized and unique per environment: a request for an email address already on the waitlist returns the existing entry unchanged (still with status `201`) and does not send another confirmation email. If a user with the email address already exists in the environment, the request fails with the code `user_already_exists`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
  "additional_fields": {
    "company": "Example Corp"
  },
  "send_confirmation_email": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-waitlist-entry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The unique ID of the waitlist, or the literal `default` for the environment's default waitlist. Use `default` when adding the first entry — the default waitlist is created automatically.|
|body|body|[CreateWaitlistEntryDto](#schemacreatewaitlistentrydto)|true|none|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|The email address of the user joining the waitlist.|
|» additional_fields|body|object|false|Object containing additional key/value pairs collected with the waitlist entry. Supports up to 50 string pairs, with keys up to 40 characters and values up to 600 characters. Values are user-provided — treat them as untrusted input when rendering or exporting.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» send_confirmation_email|body|boolean|false|Whether to send the waitlist confirmation email to the user. Defaults to `false`. No email is sent when the waitlist confirmation email is disabled in the environment, even if `send_confirmation_email` is `true`.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "wl_user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
  "state": "pending",
  "approved_at": null,
  "additional_fields": {
    "company": "Example Corp"
  },
  "waitlist_id": "waitlist_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "object": "waitlist_entry"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "action_denied",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-waitlist-entry-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|[WaitlistEntry](#schemawaitlistentry)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity|[ErrorBodyWithCode](#schemaerrorbodywithcode)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearer
</aside>


`GET /webhook_endpoints`

Get a list of all of your existing webhook endpoints.

<h3 id="list-webhook-endpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `before="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects before `"obj_123"`.|
|after|query|string|false|An object ID that defines your place in the list. When the ID is not present, you are at the end of the list. For example, if you make a list request and receive 100 objects, ending with `"obj_123"`, your subsequent call can include `after="obj_123"` to fetch a new batch of objects after `"obj_123"`.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Upper limit on the number of objects to return, between `1` and `100`.|
|order|query|[PaginationOrder](#schemapaginationorder)|false|Order the results by the creation time. Supported values are `"asc"` (ascending), `"desc"` (descending), and `"normal"` (descending with reversed cursor semantics where `before` fetches older records and `after` fetches newer records). Defaults to `normal`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|normal|
|order|desc|
|order|asc|

```json
  ],
  "list_metadata": {
    "before": "we_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "after": "we_01HXYZ987654321KJIHGFEDCBA"
  }
}
```

<h1 id="workos-widgets">widgets</h1>

Widget endpoints.

## Generate a widget token

<a id="opIdWidgetsPublicController_issueWidgetSessionToken"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/widgets/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "user_id": "user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
    "scopes": [
      "widgets:users-table:manage"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /widgets/token`

Generate a widget token for a user, optionally scoped to an organization. When an organization is specified, org-scoped widgets are enabled; omitting it issues a user-only token for widgets like `UserProfile` and `UserSecurity`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
  "user_id": "user_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
  "scopes": [
    "widgets:users-table:manage"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-widget-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WidgetSessionTokenDto](#schemawidgetsessiontokendto)|true|none|
|» organization_id|body|string|false|The ID of the organization to scope the widget session to. Required when scopes are provided. Optional when issuing a token for user-only widgets (e.g. `UserProfile`, `UserSecurity`) that do not require organization context.|
|» user_id|body|string|false|The ID of the user to issue the widget session token for.|
|» scopes|body|[string]|false|The scopes to grant the widget session.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» scopes|widgets:users-table:manage|

<h1 id="workos-workos-connect">workos-connect</h1>

A unified interface that simplifies authentication and authorization across customers, partners, and external SaaS tools.

## Complete external authentication

<a id="opIdExternalAuthController_completeLogin"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.workos.com/authkit/oauth2/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "external_auth_id": "ext_auth_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
    "user": {
      "id": "user_12345",
      "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
      "first_name": "Marcelina",
      "last_name": "Davis",
      "name": "Marcelina Davis",
      "metadata": {
        "department": "Engineering",
        "role": "Developer"
      }
    },
    "user_consent_options": [
      {
        "claim": "tos_accepted",
        "type": "enum",
        "label": "Terms of Service",
        "choices": [
          {
            "value": "accepted",
            "label": "I accept the Terms of Service"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /authkit/oauth2/complete`

Completes an external authentication flow and returns control to AuthKit. This endpoint is used with [Standalone Connect](/authkit/connect/standalone) to bridge your existing authentication system with the Connect OAuth API infrastructure.

After successfully authenticating a user in your application, calling this endpoint will:

- Create or update the user in AuthKit, using the given `id` as its `external_id`.
- Return a `redirect_uri` your application should redirect to in order for AuthKit to complete the flow

Users are automatically created or updated based on the `id` and `email` provided. If a user with the same `id` exists, their information is updated. Otherwise, a new user is created.

If you provide a new `id` with an `email` that already belongs to an existing user, the request will fail with an error as email addresses are unique to a user.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "external_auth_id": "ext_auth_01HXYZ123456789ABCDEFGHIJ",
  "user": {
    "id": "user_12345",
    "email": "marcelina.davis@example.com",
    "first_name": "Marcelina",
    "last_name": "Davis",
    "name": "Marcelina Davis",
    "metadata": {
      "department": "Engineering",
      "role": "Developer"
    }
  },
  "user_consent_options": [
    {
      "claim": "tos_accepted",
      "type": "enum",
      "label": "Terms of Service",
      "choices": [
        {
          "value": "accepted",
          "label": "I accept the Terms of Service"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="complete-external-authentication-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[UserManagementLoginRequest](#schemausermanagementloginrequest)|true|none|
|» external_auth_id|body|string|true|Identifier provided when AuthKit redirected to your login page.|
|» user|body|[UserObject](#schemauserobject)|true|The user to create or update in AuthKit.|
|» user_consent_options|body|[[UserConsentOption](#schemauserconsentoption)]|false|Array of [User Consent Options](/reference/workos-connect/standalone/user-consent-options) to store with the session.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "redirect_uri": "https://your-authkit-domain.workos.com/oauth/authorize/complete?state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdGF0ZSI6InJhbmRvbV9zdGF0ZV9zdHJpbmciLCJpYXQiOjE3NDI2MDQ4NTN9.abc123def456ghi789"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "external_auth_session_already_completed",
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Request could not be processed."
}
```

<h3 id="complete-external-authentication-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ExternalAuthCompleteResponse](#schemaexternalauthcompleteresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity|[ErrorBody](#schemaerrorbody)|

<h3 id="complete-external-authentication-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|[ExternalAuthSessionAlreadyCompletedErrorBody](#schemaexternalauthsessionalreadycompletederrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[UserConsentOptionsNotSupportedErrorBody](#schemauserconsentoptionsnotsupportederrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[EmailChangeNotAllowedErrorBody](#schemaemailchangenotallowederrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[EmailNotAvailableErrorBody](#schemaemailnotavailableerrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[InvalidEmailErrorBody](#schemainvalidemailerrorbody)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|[ErrorBodyWithError](#schemaerrorbodywitherror)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateConnectionOidcOptionsDto">CreateConnectionOidcOptionsDto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateconnectionoidcoptionsdto"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateConnectionOidcOptionsDto"></a>
<a id="tocScreateconnectionoidcoptionsdto"></a>
<a id="tocscreateconnectionoidcoptionsdto"></a>

```json
{
  "discovery_endpoint": "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration",
  "client_id": "client_123",
  "client_secret": "secret_xyz",
  "redirect_uri": "https://auth.workos.com/sso/oidc/conn_externalkey/callback",
  "pkce": true,
  "token_authentication_method": "client_secret_basic",
  "jwt_signing_key_pair": {
    "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
    "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
  },
  "id_token_signature_algorithm": "RS256",
  "fetch_user_info": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|discovery_endpoint|string(uri)|true|none|The OIDC discovery endpoint.|
|client_id|string|true|none|The OIDC client ID.|
|client_secret|string|false|none|The OIDC client secret. Required for `client_secret_basic` and `client_secret_post`, and rejected for `private_key_jwt`, which authenticates with a key pair instead. This value is write-only and is never returned.|
|redirect_uri|string(uri)|false|none|A custom OAuth callback URL override. When omitted, the standard WorkOS-generated redirect URI is used.|
|pkce|boolean|false|none|Whether PKCE is enabled for the connection.|
|token_authentication_method|string|false|none|The token-endpoint client authentication method.|
|jwt_signing_key_pair|[CreateConnectionKeyPairDto](#schemacreateconnectionkeypairdto)|false|none|A key pair for WorkOS to sign `private_key_jwt` client assertions with. Only accepted when `token_authentication_method` is `private_key_jwt`; when omitted, WorkOS generates one and returns its certificate in `oidc_options.jwt_signing_certs`.|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|string|false|none|The ID-token signing algorithm.|
|fetch_user_info|boolean|false|none|Whether to fetch additional profile attributes from the userinfo endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|token_authentication_method|client_secret_post|
|token_authentication_method|client_secret_basic|
|token_authentication_method|private_key_jwt|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|ES256|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|ES384|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|ES512|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|EdDSA|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|HS256|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|HS384|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|HS512|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|PS256|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|PS384|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|PS512|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|RS256|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|RS384|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|RS512|

|first_name|string|false|none|The IdP attribute or claim the profile's `first_name` is mapped from. When omitted, the default for the connection type is used.|
|last_name|string|false|none|The IdP attribute or claim the profile's `last_name` is mapped from. When omitted, the default for the connection type is used.|
|groups|string \| null|false|none|The IdP attribute or claim the profile's `groups` are mapped from. `null` leaves the mapping unset.|
|name|string \| null|false|none|The IdP attribute or claim the profile's `name` is mapped from. `null` leaves the mapping unset.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateConnectionDto">CreateConnectionDto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreateconnectiondto"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateConnectionDto"></a>
<a id="tocScreateconnectiondto"></a>
<a id="tocscreateconnectiondto"></a>

```json
{
  "organization_id": "org_01EHWNCE74X7JSDV0X3SZ3KJNY",
  "name": "Foo Corp",
  "external_id": "acme-legacy-conn-42",
  "connection_type": "OktaSAML",
  "attribute_maps": {
    "standard_attributes": {
      "idp_id": "sub",
      "email": "email",
      "first_name": "given_name",
      "last_name": "family_name",
      "groups": "memberOf",
      "name": "displayName"
    },
    "custom_attributes": {
      "company": "company_claim"
    }
  },
  "saml_options": {
    "idp_metadata_url": "https://idp.example.com/metadata.xml",
    "acs_url": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
    "sp_entity_id": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
    "idp_entity_id": "https://idp.example.com/entity",
    "idp_sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso",
    "idp_signing_certs": [
      "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    ],
    "sp_signing_key_pair": {
      "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
      "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
    },
    "sp_encryption_key_pairs": [
      {
        "key": "-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIE...\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----",
        "cert": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nMIIC...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier for the Organization in which the Connection resides.|
|name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for the Connection. This will most commonly be the organization's name.|
|external_id|string|false|none|The customer-owned identifier for the Connection.|
|connection_type|string|false|none|The type of the Connection. Only SAML and OIDC connection types may be created. When omitted, the type is inferred from the provided options.|
|attribute_maps|[CreateConnectionAttributeMapsDto](#schemacreateconnectionattributemapsdto)|false|none|How IdP attributes or claims map onto WorkOS profile fields. Provided fields override the defaults for the connection type.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|saml_options|[CreateConnectionSamlOptionsDto](#schemacreateconnectionsamloptionsdto)|true|none|Protocol configuration for SAML connections. Mutually exclusive with `oidc_options`.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|oidc_options|[CreateConnectionOidcOptionsDto](#schemacreateconnectionoidcoptionsdto)|true|none|Protocol configuration for OIDC connections. Mutually exclusive with `saml_options`.|

<h2 id="tocS_PatchConnectionSamlOptionsDto">PatchConnectionSamlOptionsDto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapatchconnectionsamloptionsdto"></a>
<a id="schema_PatchConnectionSamlOptionsDto"></a>
<a id="tocSpatchconnectionsamloptionsdto"></a>
<a id="tocspatchconnectionsamloptionsdto"></a>

```json
{
  "idp_metadata_url": "https://idp.example.com/metadata.xml",
  "acs_url": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
  "sp_entity_id": "https://example.auth0.com/login/callback?connection=123",
  "idp_entity_id": "https://idp.example.com/entity",
  "idp_sso_url": "https://idp.example.com/sso"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|idp_metadata_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The Identity Provider metadata URL. When provided, the IdP fields and signing certificates are re-imported from the metadata document, replacing the current set. Mutually exclusive with the manual IdP fields. Set to `null` to stop tracking a metadata URL.|
|acs_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|A custom Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL override. Set to `null` to revert to the standard WorkOS-generated ACS URL.|
|sp_entity_id|string \| null|false|none|A custom Service Provider Entity ID (audience) override. Set to `null` to revert to the connection external key.|
|idp_entity_id|string|false|none|The Identity Provider Entity ID.|
|idp_sso_url|string(uri)|false|none|The Identity Provider SSO URL.|

<h2 id="tocS_PatchConnectionOidcOptionsDto">PatchConnectionOidcOptionsDto</h2>

<a id="schema_PatchConnectionOidcOptionsDto"></a>
<a id="tocSpatchconnectionoidcoptionsdto"></a>
<a id="tocspatchconnectionoidcoptionsdto"></a>

```json
{
  "discovery_endpoint": "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration",
  "client_id": "client_123",
  "client_secret": "secret_xyz",
  "redirect_uri": "https://auth.workos.com/sso/oidc/conn_externalkey/callback",
  "pkce": true,
  "token_authentication_method": "client_secret_basic",
  "id_token_signature_algorithm": "RS256",
  "fetch_user_info": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|discovery_endpoint|string(uri)|false|none|The OIDC discovery endpoint.|
|client_id|string|false|none|The OIDC client ID.|
|client_secret|string|false|none|The OIDC client secret. Required when moving the connection to `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`, and rejected for `private_key_jwt`, which authenticates with a key pair instead. This value is write-only and is never returned.|
|redirect_uri|string \| null(uri)|false|none|A custom OAuth callback URL override. Set to `null` to revert to the standard WorkOS-generated redirect URI.|
|pkce|boolean|false|none|Whether PKCE is enabled for the connection.|
|token_authentication_method|string|false|none|The token-endpoint client authentication method. Moving to `private_key_jwt` generates a signing key pair if the connection has none; its certificate is returned in `oidc_options.jwt_signing_certs` and must be registered at the Identity Provider.|
|id_token_signature_algorithm|string|false|none|The ID-token signing algorithm.|
|fetch_user_info|boolean|false|none|Whether to fetch additional profile attributes from the userinfo endpoint.|

```json
  "pkce_enabled": true,
  "request_scope_separator": " ",
  "scopes_required": false,
  "client_secret_required": true,
  "additional_authorization_parameters": {
    "prompt": "consent"
  },
  "token_body_content_type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
  "authenticate_via": "request_body"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|A descriptive name for the custom provider.|
|authorization_url|string(uri)|false|none|The provider's OAuth authorization endpoint. Required for OAuth providers; omit for `api_key` providers. Must be a static URL: `${config.…}` placeholders are resolved against a provider's declared config fields, which custom providers cannot declare.|
|token_url|string(uri)|false|none|The provider's OAuth token endpoint. Required for OAuth and `client_credentials` providers; omit for `api_key` providers. Must be a static URL: `${config.…}` placeholders are resolved against a provider's declared config fields, which custom providers cannot declare.|
|refresh_token_url|string \| null(uri)|false|none|The endpoint used to refresh tokens, if different from the token endpoint. Must be a static URL, like the other endpoints.|

|request_scope_separator|string|false|none|The separator used to join requested scopes. Defaults to a space.|
|scopes_required|boolean|false|none|Whether at least one scope must be selected when connecting an account. Defaults to `false`.|
|client_secret_required|boolean|false|none|Whether a client secret is required for this provider. Defaults to `true`.|
|additional_authorization_parameters|object|false|none|Additional static query parameters appended to the authorization request.|
|token_body_content_type|string|false|none|The Content-Type used when exchanging the token request.|
|authenticate_via|string|false|none|How client credentials are sent when exchanging authorization codes and refreshing tokens.|

<h2 id="tocS_CreateDataIntegrationDto">CreateDataIntegrationDto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacreatedataintegrationdto"></a>
<a id="schema_CreateDataIntegrationDto"></a>
<a id="tocScreatedataintegrationdto"></a>
<a id="tocscreatedataintegrationdto"></a>

```json
{
  "provider": "github",
  "ownership": "user",
  "description": "Production GitHub app",
  "enabled": true,
  "scopes": [
    "repo",
    "read:org"
  ],
  "auth_methods": [
    "oauth"
  ],
  "config": {
    "account": "myorg-myaccount"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "type": "custom",
    "client_id": "Iv1.abc123",
    "client_secret": "secret_…"
  },
  "api_key": {
    "secret": "sk-1234567890abcdef",
    "user_id": "user_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHZNVPK3SFK441A1RGBFSHRT"
  },
  "custom_provider": {
    "name": "My OAuth App",
    "authorization_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/authorize",
    "token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
    "refresh_token_url": "https://provider.example.com/oauth/token",
    "pkce_enabled": true,
    "request_scope_separator": " ",
    "scopes_required": false,
    "client_secret_required": true,
    "additional_authorization_parameters": {
      "prompt": "consent"
    },
    "token_body_content_type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
    "authenticate_via": "request_body"
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|provider|string|true|none|The provider to create a Data Integration for. For a built-in provider use its slug (e.g. `github`, `slack`). For a custom provider, this is the new provider slug and `custom_provider` must be supplied. A custom provider slug cannot shadow an existing global provider slug.|
|ownership|string|false|none|Who owns the Data Integration. `user` (the default) creates the integration users connect their own accounts to; `organization` creates the root organizations connect to. Ownership is fixed at creation, and one integration of each ownership may exist per provider. Independent of `credentials.type`.|
|description|string \| null|false|none|An optional description of the Data Integration.|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the Data Integration is enabled. Defaults to `false`.|
|scopes|[string]|false|none|The OAuth scopes to request for the Data Integration. Defaults to the provider's configured scopes when omitted.|
|auth_methods|[string]|false|none|How accounts authenticate with the provider. Defaults to `["oauth"]`. Use `["api_key"]` to declare an API key integration; `credentials` is then not required and keys are supplied per-tenant (optionally via `api_key` on this request). Use `["client_credentials"]` to declare a client-credentials integration; `credentials` is likewise not required and client credentials are supplied per-tenant.|
|config|object|false|none|Provider-specific config values (e.g. a Snowflake `account`), keyed by the config field. Only fields the built-in provider declares are accepted.|
|credentials|[DataIntegrationCredentialsDto](#schemadataintegrationcredentialsdto)|false|none|The OAuth credentials to configure for the Data Integration. Required for OAuth integrations; omit when `auth_methods` is `["api_key"]`.|
|api_key|[ApiKeyInstallationDto](#schemaapikeyinstallationdto)|false|none|An optional API key to install for the first tenant on an `api_key` integration. Omit to declare a keyless integration; tenants can be added later via the per-installation API key path.|
|custom_provider|[CustomProviderDefinitionDto](#schemacustomproviderdefinitiondto)|false|none|The OAuth definition for a custom provider. Supply this to define a custom provider; omit it to create an integration for a built-in provider.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|ownership|user|
|ownership|organization|
|auth_methods|oauth|
|auth_methods|api_key|
|auth_methods|client_credentials|

<h2 id="tocS_TokenQueryDto">TokenQueryDto</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematokenquerydto"></a>
<a id="schema_TokenQueryDto"></a>
<a id="tocStokenquerydto"></a>
<a id="tocstokenquerydto"></a>

```json
{
  "client_id": "client_01HZBC6N1EB1ZY7KG32X",
  "client_secret": "sk_example_123456789",
  "code": "authorization_code_value",
  "grant_type": "authorization_code",
  "code_verifier": "code_verifier_value",
  "subject_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjMifQ.example",
  "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token",
  "organization_id": "org_01EHQMYV6MBK39QC5PZXHY59C3"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|string|true|none|The client ID of the WorkOS environment.|
|client_secret|string|true|none|The client secret of the WorkOS environment.|
|code|string(password)|false|none|The authorization code received from the authorization callback. Required when `grant_type` is `authorization_code`.|
|grant_type|string|true|none|The grant type for the token request.|
|code_verifier|string(password)|false|none|The PKCE code verifier matching the `code_challenge` sent with the authorization request. Required when the authorization request included a `code_challenge`. Must be sent in the request body.|
|subject_token|string|false|none|The OIDC ID token to exchange. Required when `grant_type` is `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`. Must be sent in the request body.|
|subject_token_type|string|false|none|The type of the subject token. Required when `grant_type` is `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`. Must be sent in the request body.|

```json
    "company": "Example Corp"
  },
  "waitlist_id": "waitlist_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",

  "updated_at": "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z",
  "object": "waitlist_user"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique ID of the waitlist entry.|
|email|string|true|none|The email address of the user on the waitlist.|
|state|string|true|none|The state of the waitlist entry.|
|approved_at|string \| null(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the entry was approved, or null if not yet approved.|
|additional_fields|object|false|none|Additional fields submitted when the user joined the waitlist. Values are user-provided — treat them as untrusted input when rendering or exporting.|
|waitlist_id|string \| null|false|none|The unique ID of the waitlist the entry belongs to.|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|true|none|An ISO 8601 timestamp.|
|object|string|true|none|Distinguishes the Waitlist User object.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|

|state|approved|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|object|string|true|none|Distinguishes the credential object.|
|auth_method|string|true|none|The authentication method for this credential. Additional values may be added in the future; handle unknown values gracefully.|
|value|string(password)|true|none|The vended secret. An OAuth access token when `auth_method` is `oauth`, the API key when `api_key`, or the client-credentials access token when `client_credentials`.|
|expires_at|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the credential expires, or `null` if it does not expire. Present for `oauth` and `client_credentials` credentials; absent for `api_key`.|
|scopes|[string]|true|none|The scopes granted to the access token. Present for `oauth` and `client_credentials` credentials; absent for `api_key`.|
|missing_scopes|[string]|true|none|If the integration has requested scopes that aren't present on the access token, they're listed here. Present for `oauth` and `client_credentials` credentials; absent for `api_key`.|
|metadata|object|true|none|Non-sensitive fields captured from the provider token response (e.g. Salesforce `instance_url`), as configured for the provider. Captured on OAuth code exchange and refresh, and on each `client_credentials` mint. A field a later OAuth refresh omits keeps its stored value. Present for `oauth` and `client_credentials` credentials; absent for `api_key`.|
|config|object|true|none|Provider-declared, non-secret config from the installation snapshot, with current defaults for unset fields. Includes both integration- and installation-scope fields; omits undeclared fields and fields marked secret. Use these values to address a per-tenant host, such as Snowflake's `account` or Zendesk's `subdomain`. Empty when no values are disclosable. Changes to integration or organization pins require reconnecting or explicitly rebinding the connection. Defaults are live and can differ from a cached token's audience until refresh or re-mint.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|

|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|

|auth_method|string|true|none|The authentication method for this credential. Additional values may be added in the future; handle unknown values gracefully.|

|expires_at|string \| null|true|none|The ISO-8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the credential expires.|

The scopes granted to a client-credentials token are governed by the connected organization's client application, so the integration's configured scopes are requests or defaults rather than guarantees.|

```json
{
```

```json
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InNzby...",
  "expires_in": 600,
  "profile": {
    "object": "profile",
    "id": "prof_01DMC79VCBZ0NY2099737PSVF1",
    "organization_id": "org_01EHQMYV6MBK39QC5PZXHY59C3",
    "connection_id": "conn_01E4ZCR3C56J083X43JQXF3JK5",
    "connection_type": "OktaSAML",
    "idp_id": "103456789012345678901",
    "email": "todd@example.com",
    "first_name": "Todd",
    "last_name": "Rundgren",
    "name": "Todd Rundgren",
    "role": {
      "slug": "admin"
    },
    "roles": [
      {
        "slug": "admin"
      }
    ],
    "groups": [
      "Engineering",
      "Admins"
    ],
    "custom_attributes": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "raw_attributes": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "oauth_tokens": {
    "provider": "GoogleOAuth",
    "refresh_token": "1//04g...",
    "access_token": "ya29.a0ARrdaM...",
    "expires_at": 1735141800,
    "scopes": [
      "profile",
      "email",
      "openid"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token_type|string|true|none|The type of token issued.|
|access_token|string|true|none|An access token that can be exchanged for a user profile. Access tokens are short-lived — see the `expires_in` field for the exact lifetime.|
|expires_in|integer|true|none|The lifetime of the access token in seconds.|
|profile|[Profile](#schemaprofile)|true|none|The user profile returned by the identity provider.|
|oauth_tokens|object|false|none|OAuth tokens issued by the identity provider, if available.|

<h2 id="tocS_SsoLogoutAuthorizeResponse">SsoLogoutAuthorizeResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemassologoutauthorizeresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_SsoLogoutAuthorizeResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSssologoutauthorizeresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsssologoutauthorizeresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "logout_url": "https://auth.workos.com/sso/logout?token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9",
  "logout_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJwcm9maWxlX2lkIjoicHJvZl8wMUdXUTFHMEgyRk02QVNFRjBIUzEzSENXOS0zMDRrZzAzZyIsImV4cCI6IjE1MTYyMzkwMjIifQ.Wru9Qlnf5DpohtGCKhZU4cVOd3zpiu7QQ-XEX--5A_4"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|logout_url|string(password)|true|none|The URL to redirect the user to in order to log out ([Logout Redirect](/reference/sso/logout) endpoint ready to use).|
|logout_token|string|true|none|The logout token to be used in the [Logout Redirect](/reference/sso/logout) endpoint.|
